articles.title: Apple Weighs Return to Server Market with NVIDIA Networking Technology
articles.text:
Wednesday, September 16th 2026
	
									
	
	
	
Apple Weighs Return to Server Market with NVIDIA Networking Technology
Apple is reportedly considering a return to the server market, where the company was once active with its Xserve rack technology. According to The Information, Apple is developing AI-focused M-series chips, which could incorporate several NVIDIA components, including the NVLink Fusion portfolio of technologies and IP. This includes the possibility of interconnecting two or four Apple M8 Ultra chips using NVIDIA NVLink for socket-to-socket communication, while NVIDIA NVLink-C2C manages die-to-die interconnection. Currently planned for launch in 2029, this product would mark Apple's first entry into the server space since debuting Xserve in 2002 and discontinuing it in 2011. Nearly two decades later, Apple's server offering might be making a comeback, building on the success that the Mac mini and Mac Studio are experiencing among AI developers.
For instance, Apple's Mac lineup achieved a record $10.4 billion in sales last quarter, with strong demand from the AI community. Enterprises are even constructing custom racks, mounting multiple Mac Studios to set up local AI inferencing efforts. For the new server design, Apple would delegate every interconnect question to NVIDIA NVLink Fusion, while it focuses on the actual system-on-chip as before. The new rack design would target enterprises and governments, who may already be running Mac clusters locally.Readers might recall that Apple is already working on a custom AI inference accelerator with Broadcom, codenamed "Baltra." It reportedly uses TSMC's 3 nm N3E or N3P nodes and is scheduled for late 2026 or early 2027. Perhaps Apple, which also develops Apple Foundation Models (AFM), will use the "Baltra" AI accelerator to run large-scale inference and serve its massive customer base with its models using that chip, and later offer its M8 Ultra chips as standalone racks. However, for a company as secretive as Apple, schedules might change, and we could see more information in the future. With the new CEO John Ternus at the helm, hardware offerings might expand significantly.

That aside, if they're entering the server market, their support needs to be better than what it was back in Jobs' era
2. Better scaling and performance for their on-prem hardware
It's unlikely that they'll enter the server market at all.
Enterprises want support, not just hardware that blows their minds performance wise.
Apple has tons of third-party hardware in their own datacenters and he undoubtedly understands that connecting a Mac to the rest of the equipment is the bottleneck hence the selection of NVLink as a possible solution (for these time being).
If Apple wanted to market a standalone server they could have squashed the Mac Studio into a 1U rack pizza box three years ago and shipped it.
John probably said to himself, “the devs who are buying up Mac Studios want easier connectivity to the rest of the data center.” That’s the issue, the form factor not as much.
Working backwards from the customer experience back to the hardware design is a classic Steve Jobs approach. Don’t build hardware then try to figure out how to sell it and to whom.
He did this with the MacBook Neo. He pictured a certain class of users and worked backwards to the hardware and ended up with a notebook powered by a smartphone SoC.
There are many people on tech discussion forums like TPU who don’t understand the Neo. That’s because they don’t understand that there’s a planet full of people who have different usage cases than them. John Ternus gets it.

Apple already has a lot of customers who are buying high-spec Mac Studios and Mac minis for AI development. The demand is already there. Mac minis have been present in data centers since their early years and yes there are still companies that provide this service (Mac Mini Vault is one).
It's up to each business to decide what their product mix should be and to adapt to an ever changing market if they want to survive, both short term and long term. Nintendo still makes hanafuda playing cards like they did at their founding in the 19th century but today they make more revenue from Switch software and Pokémon cards.
This is just an exploratory phase just like Apple's self-driving vehicle never hit the market. But for sure Apple will learn something they can take away from this even if this product never launches.

articles.title: Google corrige une faille zero-day activement exploitée sur les Pixel
articles.text:
Google vient de publier une grosse mise à jour de sécurité pour ses Pixel. Au programme, 110 vulnérabilités corrigées, dont une faille du modem déjà exploitée dans des attaques ciblées.
Les propriétaires de Pixel ont intérêt à ne pas trop traîner avec la mise à jour de septembre. Google vient de corriger CVE-2026-58704, une vulnérabilité de gravité élevée touchant le modem cellulaire et pour laquelle l’entreprise dit avoir repéré des signes d’exploitation « limitée et ciblée ». Elle permet à un attaquant d’élever ses privilèges sur l’appareil sans aucune interaction de la victime.
La solution tout-en-un pour protéger votre entreprise
Votre petite entreprise a de grandes ambitions. Protégez-là contre les pirates. Et développez sereinement votre activité !
Une attaque sans clic, mais pas depuis n’importe où
Dans le détail, CVE-2026-58704 résulte d’une erreur de logique dans la gestion des permissions du modem. Son exploitation peut permettre de contourner des autorisations et d’obtenir des privilèges plus élevés sur le Pixel visé, sans clic, téléchargement ni lancement d’application de la part de la victime.
La faille n’est toutefois pas exploitable depuis n’importe quel point d’Internet. Elle nécessite un accès dit « adjacent » au réseau de la cible : l’attaquant doit pouvoir atteindre l’appareil depuis un environnement réseau ou radio directement lié à celui-ci, par exemple à proximité de la victime ou depuis un même réseau local.
Ces conditions limitent les possibilités d’une attaque opportuniste à grande échelle, mais n’écartent pas le risque pour des cibles choisies à l’avance. Google n’a pas donné davantage de détails sur la méthode employée dans les attaques observées, ni sur l’identité des victimes ou des responsables.
Plus de 100 failles corrigées dans la même mise à jour
CVE-2026-58704 est la seule vulnérabilité du lot pour laquelle Google signale une exploitation active, mais le bulletin de septembre est particulièrement chargé. Au total, 110 failles sont corrigées sur les Pixel, dont 12 vulnérabilités permettant une exécution de code à distance et 89 pouvant conduire à une élévation de privilèges. Plusieurs sont classées critiques ou de gravité élevée.
Toutes sont corrigées avec le patch de septembre, que Google déploie sur l’ensemble des Pixel encore pris en charge. Vous pouvez lancer la mise à jour depuis Paramètres > Sécurité et confidentialité > Système et mises à jour > Mise à jour de sécurité. Pensez ensuite à redémarrer votre appareil pour appliquer le correctif.

articles.title: La gente se está tomando tan en serio Hyrox que ya hay ganadores de competiciones cagándose encima
articles.text:
Hasta hace unos días Joanna Wietrzyk era una joven promesa del atletismo australiano, talentosa, resistente pero prácticamente desconocida fuera de los circuitos de Hyrox, una competición fitness que lleva años expandiéndose con fuerza por el planeta. Eso (repetimos) hasta hace unos días. El sábado, mientras Wietryzk participaba en un torneo en Pekín, su cuerpo no aguantó más y se cagó encima en plena prueba. Las cámaras la inmortalizaron mientras corría y saltaba con los pantalones sucios y las heces escurriéndoseles por los muslos.
La polémica (claro) está servida.
El poder de una imagen. Si Joanna Wietrzyk hubiese colapsado lejos de las cámaras (en caso de que eso sea posible hoy en día) probablemente su historia habría sido distinta; pero cuando el pasado 12 de septiembre su vientre se soltó mientras participaba en una prueba de Hyrox en Pekín estaba rodeada de móviles y fotógrafos que no dudaron en captar la escena. Esas imágenes se viralizaron y hoy medio mundo la ha visto correr y dar saltos con las mallas, las piernas y las zapatillas manchadas con sus propias heces. Como si no hubiera pasado nada.
An Australian competitor at HYROX Beijing suffered sudden fecal incontinence mid-race due to intense physical stress — but still pushed through and finished strong.
Race organizers confirmed they immediately isolated and disinfected the affected area, disposing of equipment and… pic.twitter.com/xWSKl6m3A3
Y saltó la polémica. Las imágenes muestran tres cosas. La primera es que, probablemente por el esfuerzo, Joanna Wietrzyk no pudo contenerse y acabó yéndose de vientre. La segunda y tercera (menos obvias, pero más importantes) es que, a pesar de haber sufrido ese percance, la australiana decidió seguir compitiendo y la organización no pareció ver ningún problema en ello.
Lo primero fue un accidente involuntario, uno particularmente escatológico, pero nada del otro mundo. Lo segundo y tercero sí resulta mucho más polémico.
Y eso, ¿por qué? Porque esas decisiones afectaron al resto de atletas que competían. Desde el sábado gran parte de la conversación se ha centrado en la responsabilidad personal de Wietrzyk y, sobre todo, de la de la organización de Hyrox. Como se puede ver en los vídeos, las pruebas son individuales, pero los deportistas usan instalaciones y material que comparten con otros compañeros. Por ejemplo, a Wietrzyk se la puede ver ya manchada cargando con kettlebells, lanzando balones medicinales y corriendo por pistas junto a otros atletas.
¿Era seguro para ellos? ¿Debió apartar el jurado a Wietrzyk para no poner en peligro a los otros competidores? ¿Influyó el hecho de que la joven no sea una deportista cualquiera, sino una estrella emergente que posee el récord mundial en la prueba individual femenina? Son preguntas interesantes porque Wietrzyk, originaria de Melbourne y de 22 años, acudió a Pekín invitada para competir en el grupo de élite en la categoría de 16 a 24 años. Y no le fue mal. A pesar del incidente, ganó la prueba con una marca de 61 minutos y 23 segundos.
During the HYROX Beijing fitness race, Australian athlete and world record holder Joanna Wietrzyk reportedly suffered a bowel incontinence incident mid-race but continued competing and went on to win the event.
Some spectators compared the case with an earlier incident in which… pic.twitter.com/A7UuwYk8oT
"O lo das todo o te vas a casa". Lo ocurrido en Pekín ha generado tal controversia que tanto la atleta australiana como los organizadores de la prueba se han pronunciado. La primera, Joanna Wietrzyk, compartió poco después del torneo un selfie que la mostraba tendida en lo que parecía una cama de hospital con una vía en el brazo. Junto a la imagen, el texto "Go hard or go home they say… a win is a win" ("O lo das todo o vete a casa, como se suele decir… una victoria es una victoria"). Esa publicación de Instagram acabó eliminada.
"Hyrox cometió un error". La reacción más importante ha sido la de Moritz Fürste, cofundador de Hyrox, quien colgó un comunicado en Instagram en el que reconoce que la organización no estuvo a la altura. "Pido disculpas a todos los que se han visto afectados directa o indirectamente, así como a todos aquellos que han considerado que no gestionamos la situación como debíamos", arranca.
"Hyrox cometió un error al no reaccionar de inmediato durante la carrera. Mi trabajo consiste en prever este tipo de incidentes potenciales y no lo hice. Por supuesto, hemos empezado a mejorar los procesos de los eventos y a introducir cambios en el reglamento de forma inmediata. En este momento, ya hay nuevas normas para evitar que situaciones como esta vuelvan a ocurrir", concluye Fürste, quien impulsó la competición en 2017 en Alemania con Christian Toetzke.
🏃♀️ La atleta australiana Joanna Wietrzyk sufrió una incontinencia fecal durante la competencia de HYROX en Beijing, pero siguió compitiendo y ganó
Las pistas fueron cerradas y desinfectadas y se reemplazaron las alfombras. Tras la carrera, Joanna compartió una foto desde el… pic.twitter.com/1443fCUynr
¿Medidas a tiempo? Hyrox ha aclarado también que las pistas que pudo ensuciar Wietrzyk se limpiaron en profundidad esa misma noche. Además se retiró el equipo contaminado y se reemplazó la superficie manchada. "Tras el incidente, el comité organizador acordonó y aisló de inmediato la zona y la pista afectadas y llevó a cabo una desinfección exhaustiva", insiste la organización.
Sobre el reglamento, antes del torneo chino ya penalizaba como infracciones menores el arrojar basura, sonarse o escupir en las pistas. The Telegraph desliza que ahora se ha ampliado para incluir contaminaciones por sangre, vómito, orina o heces. El objetivo: que si la organización considera que suponen un riesgo para los atletas, pueda actuar en el acto. De telón de fondo hay un debate mucho mayor y que trasciende a Hyrox: los límites del deporte de alto rendimiento.
Un tropiezo en plena expansión. La polémica llega en un momento dulce para Hyrox, que a pesar de ser una competición relativamente joven ha logrado expandirse tras la pandemia. Sus responsables aseguran que se ha convertido en el deporte fitness "de mayor crecimiento" y ya organizan eventos en 11 países con miles de gimnasios afiliados. La clave está en su propuesta: una combinación de running con ejercicios funcionales, como remo, burpees o movimientos con peso.
Lo ocurrido en China empaña esa expansión. En redes hay usuarios que reconocen sentirse defraudados con la organización y se preguntan si, una vez reconocido el error, Hyrox no debería devolver el dinero de las inscripciones o compensar a los atletas de alguna otra forma. "Si bien entiendo la perspectiva de la atleta, mi contrato y expectativas son con Hyrox", señala un usuario que participó en el campeonato chino, aunque en la modalidad masculina.

articles.title: Anthropic brings Cowork directly inside Claude's chat interface - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Anthropic brings Cowork directly inside Claude’s chat interface
Anthropic PBC said today it’s trying to make life simpler for its customers by merging its regular chatbot Claude with its agentic artificial intelligence tool Claude Cowork.
The merger, which went into effect immediately, came as the company introduced two new features in beta. They’re called Claude Docs and Claude Slides, and they’re being integrated with Claude alongside the broader rollout of the company’s Claude Design tool, which was also a standalone product, is now being brought right inside user’s chats too.
This seems to be part of a push toward some kind of “superapp,” or a single interface that’s designed to replace the increasingly fragmented collection of AI tools for every little thing, such as asking questions, creating images, managing files, coding and automating routine work. The idea is that users would probably rather not have to decide which specific AI product to use, or manually shuffle context across tools. Instead, they should be able to do everything in one place, with the context following automatically.
This kind of integrated experience will have the effect of creating a more direct relationship with users and help increase the time they spend using a single product, and can potentially make it easier for Anthropic to bundle different premium features into a subscription. It can also be more attractive to enterprise customers, as many businesses prefer this kind of simplicity, since it allows them to centralize employees’ AI use, and therefore retain more control.
OpenAI Group PBC is also believed to be working towards creating a kind of superapp that will fold ChatGPT, its coding agent Codex and possibly also its AI browser Atlas into one product. Again, OpenAI says the idea is to reduce tool fragmentation so that AI can just switch between answering questions, researching, coding and explaining things within one session.
Despite this, it’s notable that Anthropic’s coding agent Claude Code is still a separate product, unaffected by today’s change, at least for the time being.
Anthropic said in a blog post that before the merger, many customers would struggle to know which AI tab they should choose for a specific task. With the newly integrated experience, Claude will automatically route the user’s prompt to the most appropriate interface – either Claude Chat or Claude Cowork – so the user never has to switch tabs again. Instead, they just use a single frontend to access AI whenever they need it, the company explained.
As for the new capabilities, Claude Slides is all about creating and editing PowerPoint slides. Users will be able to draft new slides, edit them and even present them from directly within Claude, or download them as a PowerPoint or PDF file.
Claude Docs, meanwhile, is all about documents – Claude can draft sections of text or help users edit, and multiple colleagues can all collaborate on the same file in real time, before exporting them to Microsoft Word or Google Docs. These new features are being made available to Claude Pro and Claude Max subscribers first on the web, desktop and mobile. They’ll also come to Team subscribers and free users in the coming weeks.
With all of these integration, there is a risk that some users could end up paying more for their AI usage. Agentic products like Cowork are designed to reason through multistep tasks and make tool calls on behalf of their users, and this kind of thing can consume vastly more tokens than a simple chat exchange. The problem is, users are billed by token usage. So if the newly integrated Claude decides to end up routing simple questions through its agentic, tool-calling machinery, users could find themselves pushing up the compute cost without even realizing it.

articles.title: Revelan lista de dispositivos que Apple lanzaría a inicios de 2027: iPhone encabeza las opciones
articles.text:
Apple prepara una nueva oleada de lanzamientos para la primera mitad de 2027, según coinciden distintos analistas y medios especializados que siguen de cerca a la compañía de Cupertino. Entre las novedades estarían el iPhone 18, el iPhone 18e, el iPhone Air 2, un iPad Air con pantalla OLED y varias actualizaciones en la línea Mac.
El movimiento responde a un cambio de calendario que ya se hizo visible en septiembre de 2026, cuando Apple presentó el iPhone 18 Pro, el Pro Max y su primer plegable, el iPhone Duo, sin incluir el modelo estándar de la serie. Los dispositivos más accesibles quedarían así para la primavera del hemisferio norte del año siguiente.
PUBLICIDAD
Cuáles serían los iPhone de Apple para inicios de 2027
Mark Gurman, periodista de Bloomberg, ubica el lanzamiento del iPhone 18, el iPhone 18e y el iPhone Air 2 entre marzo y junio de 2027. El analista Ming-Chi Kuo coincide en situar los próximos modelos de gama baja en la primera mitad de ese año.
Para el iPhone 18 estándar se espera un chip A20 fabricado con proceso de 2 nanómetros, mayor memoria, una Dynamic Island de menor tamaño y el módem C2, de acuerdo con el resumen de rumores recogido por MacRumors.
El iPhone 18e seguiría la fórmula del actual iPhone 17e, que salió a la venta en marzo de 2026 a 599 dólares con 256 GB en Estados Unidos. Kuo publicó que el modelo de 2027 pasaría de 8 a 9 GB de RAM, un dato en el que también coincide el analista Jeff Pu.
PUBLICIDAD
Sobre la pantalla, el filtrador chino Digital Chat Station aseguró en Weibo que el 18e tendría un panel de 6,12 pulgadas a 60 Hz, sin tecnología ProMotion, mientras que la cámara trasera de 48 megapíxeles se mantendría como continuidad del modelo actual.
No hay coincidencia, en cambio, respecto al diseño frontal: algunas versiones hablan de notch y otras de Dynamic Island, sin que ninguna fuente lo confirme con firmeza. Tampoco existe respaldo documentado para el supuesto precio de 599 dólares ni para un chip de conectividad N2, datos que circulan sin atribución a un analista identificable.
La segunda generación del iPhone Air recibiría la actualización más visible del grupo. Jeff Pu, citado por MacRumors, anticipa una segunda cámara trasera de 48 megapíxeles con lente ultra gran angular, que se sumaría a la cámara Fusion ya existente.
PUBLICIDAD
El teléfono incorporaría además el chip A20 Pro, también fabricado con el proceso de 2 nanómetros de TSMC, junto con los chips N2 para conectividad inalámbrica y C2 para 5G. Conservaría, según esa previsión, la pantalla de 6,5 pulgadas, 12 GB de RAM y la cámara frontal Center Stage de 18 megapíxeles.
MacRumors sitúa su llegada en el primer trimestre de 2027, en simultáneo con el iPhone 18 y el iPhone 18e.
Además de iPhone, qué otros lanzamientos haría Apple
Además de los tres iPhone, la lista incluye un iPad Air con chip M5 y pantalla OLED, un iPad Pro con chip M6 y un iPad de entrada con funciones de Siri AI.
PUBLICIDAD
En el terreno de las computadoras figuran una MacBook Air con chip M6 y una MacBook Neo con chip A19 Pro. El paquete se completa con actualizaciones del Apple Pencil Pro y el Apple Pencil vinculadas a USB-C.
El informe no precisa fechas individuales para cada producto ni si Apple los presentará en un único evento o de forma escalonada durante los primeros meses del año.
Otros dispositivos de gama alta apuntan a una ventana distinta, previa a esta oleada. Según reportó MacRumors, los MacBook Pro de 14 y 16 pulgadas con pantallas OLED táctiles ya se prueban con macOS 27.1, actualización prevista para fines de octubre de 2026.
PUBLICIDAD
Esos equipos incorporarían chips M5 Pro y M5 Max, un diseño más delgado y una Dynamic Island en lugar de la muesca actual, aunque Apple no ha confirmado nombre, precio ni fecha de presentación.
A esa misma etapa pertenecen el HomePod mini con Siri AI, el Apple TV con Siri AI, dos MacBooks de gama alta con panel táctil, un iPad Mini, un nuevo iMac y una actualización adicional del MacBook Pro, según había adelantado previamente Gurman.
La compañía tampoco ha confirmado ninguno de los nombres comerciales, especificaciones o fechas mencionados por estos analistas y medios para el bloque de la primavera de 2027.

articles.title: SteamOS is Getting Native NVIDIA GPU Driver Support
articles.text:
Wednesday, September 16th 2026
	
									
	
	
	
SteamOS is Getting Native NVIDIA GPU Driver Support
Valve is officially adding NVIDIA GPU driver support to SteamOS, as confirmed by the company's software developer Pierre-Loup Griffais. Until now, AMD has been the primary choice for SteamOS, both for CPUs and GPUs, since all of Valve's products are based on AMD hardware. However, this is changing as Valve aims to expand SteamOS to more PCs, allowing gamers to realize the Steam Machine dream on their own hardware, even if it is based on a different GPU manufacturer. When IGN asked Valve's developer about the progress of NVIDIA driver support, the response was:
Pierre-Loup Griffais for IGNYeah, we're working on it hard... We've done a few things like we've enabled the driver now in the main tree of SteamOS, so you can get things to light up on certain generations, but in terms of the performance difference between that driver and where the state of the art is, there's definitely still a little bit of a rift that we're trying to work on, but it's getting better day-to-day.
Most Linux-based operating systems support NVIDIA drivers, but they are usually not the latest releases. NVIDIA is also working to ensure that most GPUs can operate on Linux without issues. Since Valve relies on Arch Linux as the base layer for SteamOS, the rolling release cycle and Valve's upstreaming efforts could benefit almost everyone running NVIDIA GPUs on Linux-based OS, even if they don't use SteamOS. This development is a significant step toward greater compatibility, especially for new Linux gamers.
		
		Source:
				IGN

We've done a few things like we've enabled the driver now in the main tree of SteamOS, so you can get things to light up on certain generations, but in terms of the performance difference between that driver and where the state of the art is, there's definitely still a little bit of a rift that we're trying to work on, but it's getting better day-to-day.

Not a Linux fan by any means, but this is a great step forward. Very rarely I will run into a hiccup, but even the Beta channel is generally as stable as always running the latest patches in Windows for me.
That is to say, SteamOS and Windows are both quite stable.
If something funky does work it's way into an update, MS and Valve both seem to get things patched back up in quite short order :toast:
I don't know, with the insane prices now, the best bet is to just wait it out I guess so you aren't flushing your money for no reason.
Then we're left with Nvidia's open source modules + proprietary userland stack, or Nova+Mesa. The latter is far from prime time, so I don't think it'd be the case.
OTOH, from their sources I see that they have some nvk packages bundled since at least July 2026:
steamdeck-packages.steamos.cloud/archlinux-mirror/sources/jupiter-main/?C=M&O=D
So it could just be nouveau + nvk after all, and it'd explain the lacking performance.
I could not be bothered to download the kernel and firmware packages to check it out for myself.SteamOS did not, Linux itself does. Valve did not enable it by default, since it did not make sense given their current hardware offerings.No, not really. They're slowly enabling some stuff, but it's not as simple or usable as AMD, or just using another distro.That "using tools" part might be mostly because Bazzite is meant to be immutable (just like SteamOS). Maybe a distro like CachyOS could make your experience easier.That's a lie, there are 3 different open source drivers: Nova, Nouveau and Nvidia's own open modules:
github.com/nvidia/open-gpu-kernel-modulesNouveau is shitty perf-wise for any modern-ish GPU (900 series and later), and good enough for older ones (700 and older, which support reclocking).
There's also Nova, which is meant for GSP-enabled GPUs (Turing and newer), but it's far from usable as a daily driver.
And Nvidia also has their own open kernel modules, which I've linked above (also only works with turing and newer).
The "stable" way to use modern Nvidia GPUs in Linux is with Nvidia's open kernel modules (which I have linked before), and are not related to Nouveau. Those require GSP support, and the userland drivers are closed source.
I'm not including firmware stuff in the discussion since pretty much all GPUs from the past 10+ years require a proprietary firmware to work.
At the moment I have the open kernel drivers installed (nvidia-open) in Arch at kernel 7.2. I was considering trying out Nouveau at first but development seemed slow.
This addresses the 90% of the home market “normal” people. All those people that bought Best Buy computers with Nvidia GPUS are a huge market. Make it as easy to install as the Steam client is and a crapton of people will switch. Valve just needs to reduce the friction of switching and people will switch in droves. I’m one of them.
It isn't that difficult to install the Nvidia driver, regardless. Even on Fedora, which is probably one of the hardest options, you just paste a couple of commands (enable repo and install driver, which then auto-compiles a kernel module). Nvidia GPUs do typically suffer a higher (gaming) perf penalty from the swap to Linux than AMD cards do. On average, based on all the benchmarks I've seen, you can expect a 5-10% penalty on AMD gpus in Linux, and 10-15% on Nvidia. The penalty isn't inconsiderable, but it also isn't crippling; certain games can even perform better in Linux.
And of course, if you want to do CUDA stuff, Nvidia + Linux can be a fantastic combination, sometimes superior to Windows, and vastly superior to AMD on any OS.
I still barely favor AMD gpus for general purpose Linux users, but it drives me up a wall when I see e.g. Redditors screaming at newbies that they need to ditch their perfectly functional Nvidia GPUs before they commit to Linux. That isn't fair at all; nor is it constructive; nor is it accurate. Certainly not anymore. If you're tempted to try it out, don't let internet hearsay dissuade you.
- 700 series and older do not require firmware at all and nouveau can function almost as good as the older, proprietary driver for those.
- 900 & 1000 series have signed firmware, and nouveau is not able to properly use this firmware in order to adjust the GPU's clock speeds, meaning that performance sucks (since then nouveau's development has slowed down quite a lot)
- 2000 series and onwards have the GSP, and lots of the features that were previously in the kernel driver were moved onto the GSP, meaning that the new open kernel driver is almost a shim over the GSP. And since the kernel driver is now open and that interactions with the GSP are way simpler, nouveau is now able to make better use of the GPUs, but it needs to pick up on development lots of things, both feature as well as performance-wise, and this also applies to the userland drivers which were also kinda set aside for quite some time.
With that said, nouveau interacts with the GSP/firmware in order to submit stuff to the GPU, and userland drivers (mesa's suite, with opengl, opencl, vk, etc etc) interact with nouveau as an abstraction to those high-level APIsIt doesn't really "have parts", but it used the open driver as a reference on how to interact with the GSP for the newer GPUs.Same (but I still need to Syu):
No reason to try out nouveau other than for curiosity or for personal ethical reasons (like preferring a fully FOSS stack), performance and feature-parity will both be subpar.
As for the article, it's great news! When it happens, I will exclude lacking proper Linux support from my list of reasons why I'm not buying Nvidia.

articles.title: 'It's possible to have a version of DLSS 5 with minimal 'AI slop' look': leaker claims AMD is already working on tech to rival Nvidia, I just hope it doesn't arrive too late
articles.text:
AMD could be working on an Nvidia DLSS 5 rival, but it'll be for next-gen RDNA 5 GPUs — and I've a feeling that may be too late
Or could a lengthy development timeframe help AMD here?
- AMD is rumored to be working on its own version of DLSS 5
- A leaker says that the neural rendering tech will be launched with next-gen RDNA 5 GPUs
- That means we could be waiting until late 2027 or 2028 to see this debut, which might leave AMD lagging behind Nvidia considerably
AMD could be working on its own take on Nvidia's DLSS 5, and apparently this alternative attempt at neural rendering will be for its next-gen RDNA 5 graphics cards.
VideoCardz spotted that a known leaker in the GPU field, Kepler L2, posted on the Anandtech forum in a discussion around RDNA 5 speculation to say that: "AMD will have their own version of 'Neural Lighting' like DLSS5 next-gen."
Kepler then clarified that he didn't mean a version of Ray Reconstruction, but a take on DLSS 5 (neural rendering), and that next-gen RDNA 5 GPUs would be required because "this stuff is pretty heavy" (as in resource-intensive).
In a further post, Kepler elaborated: "There's a lot of issues with Nvidia's approach [with DLSS 5], but it's possible to have a version of this with minimal hallucinations and 'AI slop' look."
He then suggests a way that AMD could work its version to improve on DLSS 5, including giving the AI "direct access to 3D game data such as geometry, ray data, depth buffers, materials, etc so it doesn't have to guess and can accurately know how each object in a scene should interact with light."
Kepler's outline of a proposed alternative for AMD would have a separate model (AI) for lighting improvements, and another different model solely for the shading of complex surfaces. DLSS 5 bundles these together with its neural rendering system, and adds color-grading on top — to adopt what the AI judges as more natural colors — which Kepler advises that AMD should dispense with entirely.
Analysis: a race against time – or a chance to get it right?
I won't pretend to be able to critique what Kepler is suggesting as an alternative for AMD and the technical nuances therein, except to say that the idea is clearly to achieve a result that looks less like it's been 'messed' about with by AI and minimizes any 'slopification' therein — preserving more of the original artistic intent.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
And that seems a laudable goal, of course, and it also brings up how AMD is in an interesting position here in lagging behind Nvidia with its graphics tech (which has, of course, been the case from the start, with FSR following DLSS — version 2.0 of Nvidia's upscaling tech was already in play, in fact, when FSR 1.0 arrived). Team Red can sit back for now and see how DLSS 5 plays out, as more games emerge that use it, and gauge the reaction of gamers, and forge its own neural rendering tech to tackle any perceived weaknesses.
The performance hit will be an obvious area to target, and if AMD can bring that down — it's substantial with DLSS 5 as it is now — that will obviously be a big win. That said, I'd expect Nvidia will be working with some haste to make DLSS 5 more performant, and as with DLSS 1, the tech will be improved considerably by the time Team Red has its own version out.
This is the other side of the equation here, where Nvidia could win out. With RDNA 5 GPUs not expected to arrive for at least a year, and quite possibly longer (the RAM crisis isn't helping), there's quite a lengthy timeframe on any AMD rival to DLSS 5. By the time it arrives, DLSS 5.5 may be in town with considerable improvements in tow. There's already been a notable turnaround in the perception of DLSS 5 with its official launch (compared to Nvidia's sneak preview earlier this year).
This is, of course, assuming AMD is indeed working on its own neural rendering technology, but I'd be surprised if this wasn't the case. For now, though, the word of a single leaker needs to be thoroughly seasoned, as ever, even though it's believable enough that Team Red would be aiming to use this on RDNA 5 graphics cards.

articles.title: HP détaille enfin son premier modèle RTX Spark : l'OmniBook Ultra 16
articles.text:
Trois bons mois après le Computex et l’annonce des puces RTX Spark, HP détaille enfin son premier PC portable équipé des nouvelles solutions de NVIDIA : l’OmniBook Ultra 16. Un modèle très haut de gamme, dévolu à l’IA locale, à la création et au gaming, que l’on peut enfin découvrir sous toutes les coutures.
Après ASUS (avec ses ProArt P14 et P16), Lenovo (et ses Yoga Pro 9n), Microsoft (et son Surface Laptop Ultra) ou encore Acer (et son SFF RTX Spark, sous une forme très différente), c’est à présent HP qui détaille son premier ordinateur animé par une puce NVIDIA RTX Spark. Son nom ? L’OmniBook Ultra 16.
Un châssis rudement élégant
Si les lignes de ce nouveau modèle vous rappellent quelque chose, c’est normal, on y retrouve, en plus grand, le style de l’OmniBook Ultra 14 : un ultraportable élégant lancé en début d’année et que nous avions eu l’occasion de tester en juin. Avec son Ultra 16, HP exploite néanmoins un nouveau design thermique, inspiré par ce que l’on trouve habituellement plutôt sur les PC portables gaming fins et légers, avec charnière déportée et un châssis conçu pour optimiser la circulation de l’air et le refroidissement… Sans générer trop d’embonpoint. L’OmniBook Ultra 16 s’en tient ainsi à 1,57 cm d’épaisseur seulement et 2,22 kg, ce qui s’annonce appétissant (à première vue) pour un modèle de 16 pouces.
Comme la plupart des autres PC portables RTX Spark, l’OmniBook Ultra 16 s’appuie autrement sur une dalle OLED tactile 2,8K (2880 x 1800 pixels) et 120 Hz couvrant à 100 % l’espace DCI-P3 et montant à 500 cd/m2 en luminance SDR (1100 cd/m2 en HDR). On y retrouve une webcam 5 Mpx, ainsi que des connectiques axées sur : deux ports USB Type-C (40 Gbps), deux ports USB Type-A (10 Gbps), une prise casque et un lecteur de cartes microSD. HP mise par ailleurs sur un modem Wi-Fi 7 / Bluetooth 6.0 pour ce modèle.
Les deux saveurs de RTX Spark sont au menu
Sous le capot, pas de surprise, on retrouve une puce RTX Spark couplée à 32, 64 ou 128 Go de mémoire vive LPDDR5x (9400 MT/s) en fonction de la configuration choisie. Comme sur plusieurs modèles concurrents, HP mise ici sur les deux moutures du nouveau SoC de NVIDIA, équipées de 18 ou 20 cœurs CPU et de 6144 ou 5120 cœurs CUDA pour le GPU. L’utilisateur aura donc le choix des armes, tandis que HP se ménage des marges de manœuvre pour limiter (un peu) le prix de son premier modèle RTX Spark.
L’appareil embarque quoi qu’il en soit une batterie de 99 Wh, quelles que soient les options choisies, ainsi qu’un maximum de 2 To de SSD M.2 PCIe Gen 4 (ou 1 To de SSD PCIe Gen 5).
Pour l’instant, HP France ne communique pas de prix pour son nouvel OmniBook Ultra 16. On sait simplement que l’appareil sera commercialisé cet automne, sans plus de détails à ce stade. Un tarif salé est néanmoins attendu, même en prix de départ.
Source : Communiqué de presse HP France

articles.title: La familia de Paul Walker se pronuncia sobre el posible regreso del actor a 'Fast & Furious' mediante IA: "Lo que Meadow desee"
articles.text:
Trece años después de su muerte, Paul Walker sigue siendo inseparable de la saga 'Fast & Furious'. Por eso no es de extrañar que su antiguo compañero de reparto, Vin Diesel, quiera traerlo de vuelta en la película final, 'Fast Forever', sino que muchos quieran volver a verlo por última vez. La IA podría hacerlo realidad, pero con una condición
Ahora sí hay una vía: la IA. Existiría una posibilidad nueva de reencontrarse con Paul Walker en el próximo film de la saga. Su hermano Cody Walker acaba de explicar que la inteligencia artificial podría hacerlo realidad, como ya se ha visto en otras tantas ocasiones. Eso sí, con una condición.
"La IA no era nada en 2014". En una entrevista reciente con Entertainment Weekly, Cody Walker señaló que hoy existen vías y recursos para traer de vuelta a su hermano que hace más de diez años no existían: "La IA no era nada en 2014, hoy podrían hacerlo. Hay años de material de otras películas de 'Fast' que nunca se usó. Son los mejores de la industria, pueden encontrar la manera".
La última palabra es de Meadow. Cody Walker, no obstante, no lo ve como algo que le corresponda decidir a él, sino a Meadow, la hija de Paul Walker: "Mi postura es que eso lo decide Meadow; es su padre. No tengo ningún interés en hacerlo. Me encanta cómo su personaje abandonó la franquicia. No lo mataron, no hicieron nada cursi. Es maravilloso que Brian esté criando a sus hijos. Pero si quieren [traerlo de vuelta], si Meadow lo desea, no me necesitan a mí ni a Caleb".
Cody y Caleb ya pusieron el cuerpo. Ambos ejercieron en el pasado de dobles de su hermano fallecido en 'Fast & Furious 7'. En 2018, los dos comentaron que se imaginaban regresando una vez más a la franquicia, pero parece que Cody habría cambiado de opinión.
Vin Diesel lleva tiempo empujando. El actor se ha pronunciado en varias ocasiones a favor de recuperar a Brian, el personaje de Paul Walker, en 'Fast Forever' y reunirlo con su Dom una última vez. Si eso sucederá de verdad, y si la IA tendrá algo que ver, es algo que habrá que seguir esperando para saber.
Cuándo llega 'Fast Forever'. Hasta que la película se estrene en cines todavía queda un buen rato: está programado para el 16 de marzo de 2028. Mientras tanto, siempre es buen momento para revisitarlas todas. En particular, la primera, la segunda y la tercera. Son las mejores y de esta burra no me baja nadie.

articles.title: Iran snoops on enemies of the state with Chosen Brick malware controlled using messaging apps
articles.text:
Iran snoops on enemies of the state with Chosen Brick malware controlled using messaging apps
Journalists, dissidents and activists were among the targets
- UK NCSC, FBI, and Dutch AIVD warn Iran is using Chosen Brick malware against dissidents and journalists
- Malware steals files, captures audio, grabs WhatsApp/Telegram data, and can wipe systems entirely
- Operatives rely on social engineering; agencies urge awareness, MFA, updates, and endpoint monitoring
Iranian hackers are targeting “enemies of the state”, both local and foreign, with advanced malware capable of spying on the victims and stealing their sensitive files, experts have warned.
This is according to a new security advisory, published jointly by the UK National Cyber Security Centre, the FBI, and the Netherlands’ General Intelligence and Security Service (AIVD), which noted how Iranian operatives would first do extensive research into their victims - dissidents, activists, and journalists - deemed a risk to the regime.
After learning as much about their targets as possible, they reach out via social media, either as someone the victims know, or as technical support for the platform they’re currently using, engaging in extended conversation until the victim lowers their guard. At one point, the attackers will try to share a piece of malware with the victims, tracked as Chosen Brick.
A thousand victims
This malware, designed primarily for the Windows platform, has a long list of capabilities, including enumerating running processes and system information, capturing screen content, enabling the microphone to capture audio content, capturing a copy of Telegram and WhatsApp data from web browsers, downloading additional files and malware, deleting files, stealing email content, and ultimately - wiping the entire computer system. The operatives communicate with the malware using Telegram, it was said.
“Iran almost certainly uses cyber activity to support the repression of individuals who are seen as a threat to the regime, such as dissidents, activists and journalists,” the three agencies said in the report. “In some cases, the Iranian intelligence services have plotted to kidnap or conduct lethal operations against individuals internationally, who they perceive as enemies of the regime.”
In the advisory, the three agencies said the best defense is to simply be more aware of social engineering. However, there are also a few technical mitigations that can help, including following NCSC advice on staying safe online, keeping all devices up-to-date (ideally through automatic updates), using antivirus software, and not disabling smart screen warnings on file downloads.
Finally, it would be wise to enable phishing-resistant MFA, make sure devices are managed with appropriate controls, turn on email scanning, deploy endpoint and network monitoring, and conduct a search for the IoCs.

articles.title: Euro-Office chega ao PC para desafiar a Microsoft • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Euro-Office chega ao PC para desafiar a Microsoft
Projeto visa a soberania digital europeia. Versão para desktop deve ser disponibilizada para download nas próximas semanas.
Resumo
- A Nextcloud lançou o Euro-Office, uma suíte de aplicativos de código aberto para desafiar a Microsoft, com versão para desktop prevista para as próximas semanas.
- O Euro-Office permite a colaboração em documentos, tanto no aplicativo de desktop quanto na interface web, mantendo a sincronização entre os usuários.
- A suíte suporta formatos como DOCX, XLSX, PPTX, PDF, ODT, ODS e ODP, e visa ampliar o uso de tecnologias abertas na Europa, seguindo esforços de órgãos públicos.
Três meses após a chegada aos navegadores, o Euro-Office, suíte de apps de código aberto alternativos ao Microsoft Office, ganhará um aplicativo para desktop. A novidade foi anunciada pela Nextcloud, uma das empresas envolvidas no projeto, nesta quarta-feira (16/09).
O programa será integrado aos recursos de colaboração do Nextcloud e permitirá trabalhar nos mesmos documentos a partir do aplicativo instalado no PC ou da interface web. A versão deve ser liberada nas próximas semanas.
Euro-Office integra edições no PC e na web
O novo aplicativo mantém as funcionalidades básicas do Euro-Office para navegadores, permitindo a abertura e edição de arquivos sem perder a sincronização com os demais usuários. Isso permite que pessoas trabalhando no mesmo documento usem plataformas diferentes, como nas opções da Microsoft.
A Nextcloud também aproveitou a atualização para fazer mudanças no software. Segundo a empresa, o Euro-Office ficou mais rápido no processamento de comandos e ganhou novos mecanismos de filtragem de pastas. As miniaturas dos documentos também foram aprimoradas para facilitar a identificação dos arquivos.
A base do Euro-Office, porém, é alvo de polêmica. Mantenedores do OnlyOffice acusam o fork da coalizão europeia de violar condições da licença AGPLv3 e regras de propriedade intelectual, entre elas a remoção de avisos legais do código original. A Nexcloud contesta as alegações.
Suíte reúne formatos da Microsoft e padrões abertos
O Euro-Office foi lançado oficialmente em 9 de junho de 2026 por uma coalizão formada pela Nextcloud, Proton, IONOS, XWiki e Office.EU. A suíte reúne ferramentas para edição de textos, planilhas e apresentações.
Entre os formatos compatíveis estão DOCX, XLSX, PPTX e PDF, além de ODT, ODS e ODP, baseados no padrão aberto OpenDocument.
A iniciativa acompanha esforços de órgãos públicos europeus para ampliar o uso de tecnologias abertas. Na Alemanha, por exemplo, o formato ODF vem sendo adotado em projetos de digitalização do setor público, enquanto a França tem migrado parte de seus computadores governamentais para Linux.

articles.title: Roborock Saros 20 Neo : Le franchisseur d'obstacles
articles.text:
Roborock Saros 20 Neo : Le franchisseur d'obstacles
Présenté à l'IFA 2026, le Roborock Saros 20 Neo pousse à l'extrême deux critères discriminants sur le marché du robot-aspirateur : le franchissement d’obstacles et la puissance d’aspiration. Avec ses 36 000 Pa et son châssis élévateur, il rebat les cartes du haut de gamme domestique.
Le robot aspirateur a longtemps buté sur une promesse difficile à tenir. Celle de l’autonomie réelle en toute circonstance. Un seuil trop haut ou un tapis épais suffisait à interrompre le cycle d’aspiration. Avec le Saros 20 Neo, qui a été dévoilé début septembre à Berlin lors de l’IFA 2026, par Roborock, la donne évolue. La puissance d'aspiration ne suffit plus à distinguer un flagship ; c'est la capacité à circuler dans un intérieur réel qui fait désormais la différence.
Un maître dans l’art du franchissement
Comment circuler là où les autres renoncent ? Par la mécanique, d'abord. Le châssis AdaptiLift 3.0 constitue l'argument central du Saros 20 Neo. Ses bras élévateurs lui permettent de franchir des seuils à double niveau pouvant atteindre jusqu’à 8,8 cm. Anecdotique ? Pas vraiment. Autour de 8 cm, c’est la hauteur sur laquelle bloque jusqu'ici la quasi-totalité des concurrents. À l'inverse, sa hauteur ramenée à 7,95 cm l'autorise à se glisser sous des meubles bas. Ceux sous lesquels les autres robots-aspirateurs ne peuvent passer et laissent les moutons et la poussière s’accumuler paisiblement. Cette double prouesse témoigne par ailleurs d’un changement de doctrine : plutôt que de cartographier les zones interdites pour les éviter, le robot cherche à les intégrer à son parcours. En ligne de mire : une couverture continue, sans intervention manuelle, qui devient l'argument commercial dominant, au moins autant que les chiffres bruts d'aspiration.
36 000 Pa : la course à la puissance
Ces chiffres bruts, justement, Roborock ne les glisse pas sous le tapis (jeu de mots !). Le Saros 20 Neo affiche une puissance d’aspiration de 36 000 Pa. Une caractéristique dont il n’a pas à rougir dans un contexte d’inflation permanente des fiches techniques sur ce segment. Couplé à un double système anti-enchevêtrement pour lequel Roborock revendique un taux nul de nœuds de cheveux, il vise clairement les foyers avec animaux. Le lavage suit la même logique intensive : pression au sol jusqu'à 14 N, eau chaude, et une station qui nettoie les serpillières à 100 °C pour limiter bactéries et odeurs. Ces spécifications techniques ont de quoi impressionner.
Un positionnement tarifaire révélateur
Reste le prix, qui en dit long sur la maturité du marché. Affiché à 1 299 euros, le Saros 20 Neo est disponible actuellement à 799 euros, quelques jours seulement après son annonce. Cette décote de 500 euros, sur un produit tout juste lancé, illustre une concurrence féroce dont vous pouvez, en tant que consommateur, tirer profit pour vous équiper d’un modèle haut de gamme au meilleur prix.
Le Roborock Saros 20 Neo est disponible sur le site officiel Roborock et sur Amazon. C’est le moment de se doter d’un vrai robot-aspirateur tout terrain !

articles.title: Ex-Infosys chief Vishal Sikka's Hang Ten raises $53M more for enterprise AI services - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Ex-Infosys chief Vishal Sikka’s Hang Ten raises $53M more for enterprise AI services
Enterprise artificial intelligence services startup Hang Ten Systems Inc. today announced it has raised $53 million in a second seed round, less than three months after announcing its first.
Hang Ten provides advisory, transformation and applied AI services, and its customers are large enterprises trying to get AI working inside their businesses. The delivery model is built on agentic code generation and a reusable library of skills, with domain experts rounding it out.
Hang Ten says that setup lets it build, change and run enterprise software well under the cost and timeline of a traditional systems integrator. Projects so far have covered software development, finance analytics and human resources, among other areas.
Founder and Chief Executive Vishal Sikka told TechCrunch that the “build part itself has basically become close to zero marginal cost, close to zero time.”
Hang Ten said the two rounds closed five weeks apart, and several contracts worth millions of dollars each were signed with global enterprises in that window. Some of those engagements are multiyear development programs. Work on a few is already finished. According to TechCrunch, Hang Ten’s customers and late-stage prospects add up to 21 large enterprises, and one of them signed a multimillion-dollar deal within 25 days of the first meeting.
The company is building applications for several functions at Saudi Arabian Oil Co., one of two customers named in the announcement. Siemens Energy AG’s wind unit Siemens Gamesa is the other. The wind turbine maker brought Hang Ten in two months ago with a short list of outcomes it needed proven. Chief Executive Vinod Philip said the startup delivered “with a quality and speed that genuinely impressed us,” and the scope of the work has since been widened.
The new capital will pay for delivery capacity on current engagements and a bigger engineering and consulting organization. Some of it goes to the platform, infrastructure and skills library. Hang Ten employs 20 to 25 people across the U.S., the Middle East and Australia, and plans to hire in Europe and India.
Sikka was chief executive of Indian information technology services company Infosys Ltd. between 2014 and 2017. Prior to that he worked at SAP SE. After leaving Infosys, he co-founded Vianai Systems Inc. in 2019, which he left in April this year to found Hang Ten.
AI “can be the most powerful amplifier we have ever built,” Sikka said in the funding announcement, adding that in the enterprise that power has to go hand in hand with reliability.
Xora Innovation Pte. Ltd., an early-stage investment platform backed by Singapore’s Temasek Holdings (Private) Ltd., led the new round. Mayfield, which led the $32 million first round, came back for this one along with Aramco Ventures. Individual backers include Intel Corp. Chief Executive Lip-Bu Tan, Micron Technology Inc. Chief Executive Sanjay Mehrotra and Yahoo co-founder Jerry Yang. Yang, a founding partner at AME Cloud Ventures, has joined the board.
Phil Inagaki, managing partner and chief investment officer at Xora, said the bottleneck in enterprise AI is implementation, which means deploying it “securely, economically and at speed.” He added that Xora sees the same urgency in Singapore and across the region.
Aramco Ventures Chief Executive Mahdi Aladel said the more closely his team looks at Hang Ten’s approach, “the more functions and use cases we find across our own operations where it would fit.” Projects at Aramco are already being scoped.
Investors have now put $85 million into the company across its two seed rounds.

In our 4.5 star review of the A8 Max, we found it "extremely powerful," noting it "ploughs through tasks in Microsoft Office and applications from the Adobe Suite without too much issue."

Connectivity is another strength. Dual 2.5G LAN ports, USB4, and 8K output support are specs you would normally expect from a larger, more expensive desktop, not a compact box small enough to VESA-mount behind a monitor.

Pricing on this specific configuration has swung fairly widely across retailers and over time, from under $900 during some promotions to over $1,000 at others. So this is a solid, verified price rather than the lowest ever recorded, but it is a real saving off the current list price.

articles.title: Samsung comienza a desplegar One UI 9 sobre Android 17. Eso sí: habrá que tener algo de paciencia
articles.text:
Las cosas de palacio van despacio y las actualizaciones de Android, a veces, también. Sin embargo, Samsung ha pillado carrerilla estos últimos años actualizando a la nueva versión de Android no sólo bastante rápido, sino también con una generosa lista de móviles compatibles.
La última es One UI 9 sobre Android 17, versión que tuvimos de serie en los plegables como el Galaxy Z Fold 8, que ahora inicia su despliegue al resto de la familia.
A continuación, vamos con las principales novedades de One UI 9, los Samsung compatibles y los tiempos, ya que aunque ahora comience el despliegue, puede que tarde unos días en llegar a tu dispositivo.
Las funciones de One UI 9
Como es habitual, una nueva versión de software llega con algunos cambios visuales y en animaciones. Con Android 17, también aseguramos las últimas mejoras en cuanto a seguridad (que se unen a Nox en muchos modelos de Samsung), pero el protagonismo absoluto de esta versión recae en la IA.
Porque hay mucha, muchísima IA que impregna prácticamente todas las novedades del sistema. Por un lado, lo realmente nuevo:
- My FanCam: se trata de una función que identifica y sigue automáticamente a una persona elegida dentro de un vídeo ya grabado, ajustando el encuadre de manera inteligente conforme cambia la escena, de forma que los momentos con movimiento se transformen en contenido listo para compartir en redes sociales sin apenas necesidad de editar. Un ejemplo es la actuación de un amigo bailando o la de un jugador dentro de un partido.
- Now Brief ahora permite personalizar el contenido de los resúmenes diarios gracias a tarjetas generativas. Podemos añadir tarjetas de salud o clima para adaptar mejor el resumen a aquello que nos interesa de verdad.
- Ajustes ahora tiene un apartado de "Garantía y cuidado" que centraliza el soporte del dispositivo. Desde ahí, podemos revisar la cobertura de la garantía de los dispositivos móviles vinculados, hacer un diagnóstico, ver la estimación del coste de reparación, gestionar Samsung Care+ o pedir asistencia oficial.
También hay cambios y novedades en funciones que ya estaban disponibles:
- Now Nudge: ahora ofrece información y sugerencias más contextuales. Por ejemplo, la organización de planes de un chat, que ahora nos permite guardar desde ahí mismo una ubicación o consultar detalles de una reserva en un restaurante, por ejemplo.
- Estudio Creativo: cuando la app se da cuenta de que se acerca una efeméride como puede ser un cumpleaños de un contacto, Estudio Creativo sugiere la creación de una imagen o una felicitación.
- Intérprete: se ha mejorado el modo de conversación para que sea más fluido gracias a traducciones más rápidas. Si además tenemos unos Galaxy Buds compatibles, la reproducción de audio es más ágil para que la conversación tenga menos pausas y el diálogo sea más natural. Además, ahora tendrá una 'memoria' para ver conversaciones pasadas.
- Escaneado de documentos: han añadido mejoras al escaneado de documentos como esas páginas curvadas en libros o de hojas con las esquinas dobladas. Además, se ha mejorado la función de borrado de dedos para que el escaneo sea más limpio.
- Grabadora de voz: los resúmenes de las notas de voz ahora se organizan de otra forma, con tablas y encabezados que permiten localizar de un vistazo la información más importante.
Por otro lado, también hay mejoras en seguridad:
- Now Brief ahora tiene Security Brief, que reúne información sobre seguridad y privacidad como avisos de malware, apps de origen desconocido o esas apps que piden demasiados permisos para funcionar. De esta forma, el usuario está más informado sobre los posibles riesgos y puede tomar medidas.
- Alertas de privacidad mejoradas que detectan posibles amenazas, como pueden ser permisos en segundo plano.
Muchas de estas funciones necesitan, eso sí, cuenta en Samsung y algunas estarán disponibles dependiendo del país. Por ejemplo, Samsung detalla que la cobertura, precio y requisitos de Samsung Care+ dependen tanto de país, la región y que en algunos casos se aplicarán tarifas de servicio.

articles.title: Freiner l'IA ? C'est non ! Pour Meta et NVIDIA, le plan d'Anthropic ne passe pas
articles.text:
Freiner sur l'IA, c'était le plan d'Anthropic, approuvé par Elon Musk et Sam Altman. Toutefois, deux autres acteurs majeurs de la tech n'approuvent pas. Laissent-ils la place libre à une IA hors de contrôle ?
Les dirigeants de Meta et de NVIDIA, Mark Zuckerberg et Jensen Huang, ont exprimé leur désaccord face aux appels récents visant à réguler et à ralentir le développement des modèles d'intelligence artificielle auto-améliorables. Tous deux estiment qu'une telle intervention réglementaire n'est pas nécessaire.
Cette prise de position fait suite aux déclarations du PDG d'Anthropic, Dario Amodei, qui a préconisé une intervention gouvernementale pour inciter les entreprises du secteur à ralentir simultanément le développement de ces technologies. Dario Amodei propose un plan s'articulant autour de trois axes : le renforcement des évaluations par des tiers au sein de chaque entreprise, l'établissement de normes de sécurité en concertation avec le gouvernement américain, et la signature d'accords internationaux pour restreindre les usages potentiellement dangereux de l'IA.
La responsabilité individuelle des entreprises mise en avant
S'exprimant mardi sur la chaîne CNBC, le PDG de NVIDIA, Jensen Huang, s'est opposé à l'instauration de nouvelles règles. Il a affirmé qu'il existait déjà suffisamment de lois et de réglementations encadrant la fiabilité et le fonctionnement des produits, rendant inutile la création de nouvelles lois ou règles antitrust pour contraindre les entreprises à effectuer leurs travaux d'ingénierie avant la mise sur le marché. Jensen Huang a précisé que la sécurité demeurait importante, mais qu'il appartenait à chaque entreprise de procéder aux tests nécessaires et de retenir un produit tant qu'il n'est pas prêt.
De son côté, Mark Zuckerberg a partagé un avis similaire sur X. Tout en reconnaissant l'importance de la sécurité, le PDG de Meta soutient que la gestion des risques relève de la responsabilité de chaque acteur. Il a indiqué que Meta avait elle-même retardé de plusieurs mois le lancement de son dernier modèle, baptisé Muse, en raison de réserves internes liées à la sécurité, sans pour autant demander au reste du secteur d'interrompre ses travaux.
Mark Zuckerberg a également suggéré que les entreprises concurrentes fassent appel à davantage d'évaluateurs et de conseillers indépendants, à l'instar de ce que réalise Meta, et a souhaité le développement de ce secteur d'évaluation tierce.
Des avis partagés au sein du secteur et de la politique
La proposition formulée par le PDG d'Anthropic avait dans un premier temps reçu un accueil favorable de la part du PDG d'OpenAI, Sam Altman, d'Elon Musk (SpaceX), ainsi que du cofondateur de Google DeepMind, Demis Hassabis.
En revanche, le président américain Donald Trump s'est prononcé contre le plan d'Anthropic et contre toute nouvelle réglementation, qualifiant les inquiétudes relatives à la sécurité de l'IA de « canular ». Il a déclaré que les demandes d'encadrement étaient portées par des forces négatives mettant en avant des situations qui ne se produiront pas.
Mais qui a tout intérêt à empêcher le ralentissement de l'IA ? Certes, les patrons d'OpenAI, Anthropic, Meta et SpaceXAI, mais ces derniers proposent déjà des modèles performants. Cependant, côté NVIDIA, moins de croissance des besoins en puissance de calcul, c'est moins de revenus. La position de Jensen Huang s'explique assez facilement.

articles.title: Gnome 51 chega para continuar sendo referência no Linux; veja as novidades • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Gnome 51 chega para continuar sendo referência no Linux; veja as novidades
Ambiente de desktop Gnome 51 "A Coruña" foca em melhorias de desempenho e segurança, e em atualizações de aplicativos nativos.
O Gnome 51 é oficial. De codinome “A Coruña”, a nova versão de um dos mais populares ambientes de desktop para distribuições Linux não muda muito no visual, mas traz várias novidades funcionais e em aspectos como desempenho e segurança. Vejamos algumas delas.
Os desenvolvedores destacam que, na nova versão, o Gnome torna as animações do gerenciador de janelas Mutter mais suaves, mesmo quando há alta carga de processamento. Mas o que eu mais gostei foi a promessa de captura de tela mais rápida (uso muito esse recurso).
Ainda na parte gráfica, o Gnome 51 é capaz de memorizar o nível de brilho da tela mesmo quando houver várias reinicializações e alternâncias para um modo de HDR. Assim, você não precisa ficar reconfigurando esse parâmetro.
Mas as principais mudanças envolvem os aplicativos. O Gnome Maps agora permite baixar mapas para uso offline, bem como pode exigir horários de transporte público, por exemplo.
Já o gerenciador de arquivos nativo pode selecionar automaticamente arquivos recém-criados ou copiados para facilitar ações relacionadas, bem como exibir uma contagem de itens selecionados quando vários deles forem arrastados, sem contar que o seu desempenho foi otimizado.
Por sua vez, o visualizador de documentos Papers permite desenhar ou importar imagens de assinaturas para inserção em PDFs (com remoção de fundo), enquanto o visualizador de imagens Loupe passa a exibir mais informações de metadados, como criador, direitos autorais e perfil de cor.
As demais novidades incluem (mas não se limitam a):
Como o Gnome 51 é um ambiente de desktop, convém esperar que a novidade chegue à distribuição Linux que você usa. Um exemplo: o Fedora Linux 45 já conta com o Gnome 51, embora ainda esteja em fase beta.
O Ubuntu 26.10, a ser lançado em outubro, também contará com essa versão. O mesmo vale para futuras versões de projetos como Arch Linux, openSUSE e Manjaro Linux.
Saiba mais sobre o Gnome 51 no anúncio oficial.

articles.title: Les consommateurs font durer leur smartphone, les marques vont devoir s’y faire
articles.text:
Smartphones : malgré les nouveautés, les utilisateurs patientent désormais bien plus longtemps avant de changer d'appareil
Aux États-Unis, le smartphone tient désormais près de trois ans avant d’être remplacé. En France, les données les plus récentes racontent une histoire encore plus étonnante.
De nouveaux smartphones sortent chaque semaine, mais nos poches ne suivent plus forcément. Une étude Reviews.org menée en août 2026 auprès de 1000 adultes étasuniens estime le cycle de renouvellement à 32 mois en moyenne, contre 29 mois en 2025.
Performances, batterie, casse : les critères qui poussent à changer de smartphone
Le décalage entre l'intention et la réalité est frappant : une majorité de sondés déclarent posséder leur smartphone depuis environ 24 mois et pensent attendre encore 21 mois, soit 45 mois au total. Pourtant, ils en changent en pratique presque un an plus tôt.
Contre toute attente, la photo ne serait pas le principal déclic. Les performances arrivent en tête (21,3 %), devant l'autonomie de la batterie (19,2 %) et la casse ou la perte (14,4 %). Suivent les nouvelles fonctionnalités (9,7 %), l’envie de posséder le dernier modèle (7,9 %), les offres de reprise ou forfaits subventionnés (7,5 %), la capacité de stockage (7,1 %), les nouvelles technologies comme la 5G (6,5 %) et, enfin, l’appareil photo (4,9 %).
Le coût moyen d'un smartphone outre-Atlantique s'établit à 634 $ avec une médiane à 600 $. Environ 45 % des acheteurs paient comptant, tandis que 34 % passent par leur opérateur. Dans l’échantillon, l’iPhone pèse 58 %, contre 42 % pour Android. Chez les possesseurs de terminaux Apple, les iPhone 11 (ou modèles antérieurs) forment même la catégorie la plus représentée, à 9,4 %. À la rédaction des Numériques, nous avons d’ailleurs un véritable champion de la longévité : l'un d'entre nous utilise toujours le même terminal depuis huit ans.
Renouvellement des mobiles : les utilisateurs français encore plus patients
Le Crédoc, un organisme français de recherche sur la consommation et les modes de vie, ne fournit pas de moyenne directement comparable. Son enquête de 2025 montre toutefois que 66 % des détenteurs renouvellent leur téléphone tous les quatre ans ou moins souvent, dont 31 % tous les six ans ou davantage.
Le Baromètre du numérique 2025 va dans le même sens : 27 % des personnes interrogées gardent leur smartphone depuis au moins trois ans, contre 16 % en 2020. Seuls 21 % remplacent encore un appareil fonctionnel ; 78 % achètent neuf et 22 % se tournent vers le marché de l'occasion ou du reconditionné.
Le mouvement est donc clair des deux côtés de l’Atlantique : le renouvellement ralentit. Malgré l’IA, les zooms et autres nouveautés annuelles, la batterie, les performances et la durabilité semblent peser bien plus lourd au moment de repasser à la caisse.

articles.title: Noetive launches with $41M to bring self-improving AI to factories and logistics - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Noetive launches with $41M to bring self-improving AI to factories and logistics
Industrial artificial intelligence startup Noetive formally launched today with $41 million in seed funding.
Its software learns how a factory floor or a freight operation runs day to day, and the company says design partners in manufacturing, logistics, energy and data centers already use it.
Most AI products to date “were designed for information work living on the internet,” Chief Executive Amir Frenkel said in the launch announcement. Running a plant or a distribution network means juggling materials, machinery, labor and suppliers that never stop changing. According to Noetive, the decisions tying those together still rest on data from siloed systems that were never built to coordinate an entire business.
Noetive calls its answer an “intelligence of record.” At the core is a self-improving AI model the company refers to as a brain. The agents built on it run on top of the tools a customer already has and take on the hardest operational problems end to end. Each deployment is supposed to make the model more capable. Physical conditions reach it through a multimodal sensing pod that Noetive designs itself.
Food and beverage manufacturer Steuben Foods Inc. is one of the early partners. Its chief executive, Menachem Katz, said production planning has always been one of the most time-consuming parts of running the business because even small changes ripple across the operation. Noetive now reads both Steuben’s system data and conditions on the factory floor, and Katz said work “that once happened monthly and took a week of planning now happens daily and takes minutes.”
Meta Platforms Inc. employed Frenkel as a vice president for nearly a decade, and he has also held leadership roles at Alphabet Inc. and Amazon.com Inc. The rest of the team comes from those companies and from Fortune 500 businesses, and includes researchers who have worked on foundation models.
The funding will pay for research into self-improving AI for physical operations, the company said. Field testing happens with a curated group of design partners, and Noetive is recruiting AI researchers and full-stack engineers to expand its staff.
Eclipse Ventures led the round. Bloomberg reported in April that the firm had hired Frenkel from Meta as its first chief AI officer. Noetive took shape inside Eclipse from there, with the firm helping recruit the founding team.
Other backers in the round are Craft Ventures Management, The Westly Group, Swish Ventures, Factory, Incite Ventures, Gigascale Capital, Operator Partners and Liquid 2 Ventures. Nest co-founder Matt Rogers founded Incite, and Gigascale was started by former Meta Chief Technology Officer Mike Schroepfer. Individual investors include Meta Chief Technology Officer Andrew Bosworth, Airbnb Inc. Chief Technology Officer Ahmad Al-Dahle and the three co-founders of Decart.AI Inc.
Eclipse founder and CEO Lior Susan said the $30 trillion physical economy “has largely been left behind” by AI. “We saw an enormous opportunity to change that, and built Noetive to go after it,” he said.

articles.title: Denuvo Files Lawsuit Against Anonymous Game Cracker "voices38"
articles.text:
Wednesday, September 16th 2026
	
	
	
	
Denuvo Files Lawsuit Against Anonymous Game Cracker "voices38"
Denuvo has sued an anonymous game cracker known as "voices38," accusing them of bypassing its Anti-Tamper protection in at least 26 PC games. TorrentFreak first reported on the complaint, filed September 14 in the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of California. Denuvo wants monetary damages plus an injunction barring further circumvention of its DRM, including in games that haven't even been made yet. Denuvo doesn't own the copyrights to any of the games listed, so this isn't a copyright infringement case. It rests instead on the DMCA's anti-circumvention provisions, which prohibit bypassing digital locks placed on copyrighted works.
Named titles include Hogwarts Legacy, Black Myth: Wukong, Resident Evil Requiem, and Doom: The Dark Ages, though voices38 has apparently kept cracking games since the filing, with Persona 3 Reload and Star Wars Outlaws reportedly added to the tally. The tricky part is that Denuvo has no idea who voices38 actually is. The complaint names the defendant only as "an unknown individual or entity," alongside ten unnamed Doe defendants, pointing to Reddit, Discord, and Steam accounts it believes may be linked to the activity. Denuvo will likely need to subpoena those platforms to get anywhere close to an identity, and there's no guarantee that works out. The case is still in its early stages, and none of Denuvo's claims have been tested in court yet.

articles.title: Google corrige três falhas críticas no navegador Chrome • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Google corrige três falhas críticas no navegador Chrome
Atualização também fecha outras 39 brechas de segurança e já está disponível para Windows, macOS e Linux.
O Google corrigiu 42 vulnerabilidades no Chrome, três delas classificadas como críticas. Segundo a empresa, nenhuma delas foi explorada em ataques cibernéticos até o momento. Do total, 26 falhas foram identificadas internamente, enquanto as outras 16 foram encontradas por pesquisadores externos.
Para evitar que invasores explorem as brechas, o Google já disponibilizou uma atualização de segurança para Windows, macOS, Linux, Android e iOS.
As compilações 153.0.8010.47 e 153.0.8010.48 do Chrome para Windows e macOS, bem como a 153.0.8010.47 para Linux e Android, trazem as soluções para as vulnerabilidades. Os usuários do iOS também recebem as proteções na versão 154.0.8037.41 do navegador.
Na prática, as três falhas mais graves poderiam permitir que um invasor escapasse do ambiente isolado do navegador, conhecido como sandbox, e passasse a agir diretamente no sistema operacional da vítima. Para explorar essas vulnerabilidades, bastaria induzir o usuário a acessar uma página web adulterada.
A atualização também corrige 28 falhas de alto risco, além de diversos problemas de gravidade média e baixa. Entre os ajustes estão correções de segurança no mecanismo JavaScript e no sistema de extensões do Chrome.
O Chrome geralmente realiza o download dessas melhorias em segundo plano, mas o processo de distribuição é gradual. Para garantir a proteção imediata, uma opção é forçar o update manualmente:
Caso tenha dúvidas sobre o procedimento, o Tecnoblog tem um guia para atualizar o Google Chrome no Android, iPhone e PC. Já no Linux, a disponibilidade da atualização pode variar conforme a distribuição, como Fedora e Ubuntu. Nesses sistemas, o processo costuma ser gerenciado pelo instalador de pacotes, e não pelo menu interno do navegador.
Vale destacar que o Google passou a liberar uma nova versão do Chrome a cada duas semanas para reforçar a segurança e acelerar a chegada de melhorias aos usuários.
