articles.title: Quand arrive le nouveau Siri en France ? L’astuce pour le tester avant tout le monde sur iPhone
articles.text:
Quand arrive le nouveau Siri en France ? L’astuce pour le tester avant tout le monde sur iPhone
Le nouveau Siri dopé à l’IA n’a toujours pas de date de sortie pour la France, mais les précédentes habitudes d’Apple pourraient nous donner un indice sur son lancement. Et pour les plus impatients, une astuce existe toujours sur iPhone.
iOS 27 est maintenant disponible, mais Siri AI reste le grand absent de nos iPhone français, ainsi que de tous ceux de l’Union européenne. La faute au DMA, qui freine le déploiement des nouvelles capacités d’intelligence artificielle d’Apple sur le Vieux Continent. Pour en profiter, il faudra prendre son mal en patience, comme c’était le cas au début pour Apple Intelligence, ou opter pour la seule alternative actuelle : passer par un compte Apple étranger.
Une attente calquée sur Apple Intelligence pour Siri AI ?
Siri AI est la grande nouveauté des OS 27 d’Apple, mais se cantonne pour le moment chez nous aux Mac… et uniquement en anglais. Nos iPhone, iPad et Apple Watch ne peuvent ainsi pas y goûter tant qu’Apple et l’Union européenne n’auront pas trouvé un terrain d’entente pour se plier aux règles d’ouverture à la concurrence imposées par le Digital Markets Act (DMA).
Le plus triste dans l’histoire, c’est que la barrière de la langue va bientôt tomber, Apple ayant confirmé l’arrivée de Siri AI en français dès octobre 2026. Petit couac : seuls les pays situés hors de l’UE et de la Chine pourront en profiter. Pour espérer une ouverture dans l’Hexagone, il faudra donc attendre plusieurs mois, et pourquoi pas regarder le calendrier historique d’Apple Intelligence sous iOS 18.
Cupertino avait d’abord réservé ses nouveautés IA aux États-Unis à l’automne, avant de trouver un terrain d’entente avec Bruxelles au printemps suivant, lors du déploiement d’iOS 18.4. Le scénario le plus crédible pointe donc vers une sortie européenne de Siri AI calée vers mars ou avril 2027, lors du déploiement d’iOS 27.4.
Un contournement efficace, mais contraignant
En attendant cette échéance, qui pourrait être plus proche si Apple et l’UE se mettent plus rapidement d’accord cette fois-ci, les plus curieux peuvent contourner la restriction de Siri AI plus ou moins simplement.
Pour cela, il suffit de se connecter à un compte App Store d’un pays où cette nouveauté est disponible. Cela est notamment le cas pour le Royaume-Uni, la Suisse, Monaco, le Canada ou encore les États-Unis. Seule contrainte, il est obligatoire d’avoir un numéro de téléphone non rattaché à un autre compte Apple, voire un numéro local selon la zone géographique choisie.
La manipulation consiste ensuite à basculer la langue de l’iPhone et de Siri sur English (United States) dans les réglages, puis de se déconnecter de la rubrique Achats et abonnements de votre compte Apple afin de renseigner vos identifiants étrangers. Le bouton pour rejoindre la liste d’attente apparaîtra alors sur l’appareil dans les paramètres de Siri, permettant d’y accéder peu de temps après.
L’astuce exige néanmoins des concessions : elle suspend l’accès local à Apple Music et impose d’interagir avec l’iPhone exclusivement en anglais au quotidien.

articles.title: Anthropic wants Claude to analyze your bank account and financial data
articles.text:
Anthropic is testing a new personal finance feature called "Claude Money" that will allow you to connect your bank accounts directly to Claude and "understand your money."
AI companies coming after your finances is not a new thing, as OpenAI has a similar feature, and Anthropic appears to be catching up.
As spotted by TestingCatalog on X, Anthropic is testing the feature for the Claude app on iOS, where a new Money section has appeared alongside Chats, Code, Artifacts, Dispatch, and Cowork.
"Understand your money with Claude," the page reads. "Link your bank accounts and ask Claude about spending, plans, and more."
There's also a "Get started" button for connecting an account, although the feature does not appear to be rolling out to most users.
It's worth noting that Claude Money references showed up in the app ahead of the expected announcement, which is why details around it are quite limited.
We don't yet know which banks it will support, how accounts will be connected, or if the feature will be locked to the United States (or certain states in the country).
Claude Money looks a lot like ChatGPT Finances
As I mentioned, OpenAI already offers a similar feature called Finances in ChatGPT, which lets you connect bank accounts, credit cards, brokerages, and other financial accounts through Plaid.
When you connect your finances to ChatGPT, it can use your data to answer questions about spending, bills, subscriptions, savings, net worth, and investments.
OpenAI insists it does not train AI models on your personal data, and that it currently supports more than 12,000 financial institutions in the U.S.
Anthropic could follow a similarly limited rollout for Claude Money, and I wouldn't be surprised if the feature never rolls out in Europe due to local privacy laws.

articles.title: Shopify Drops React Native for Swift and Kotlin as AI Changes Cross-Platform Development Tradeoffs
articles.text:
Shopify recently announced it is abandoning React Native to rewrite its flagship apps in Swift and Kotlin. With the significant jump in the quality of AI models, Head of Mobile Mustafa Ali reassessed Shopify’s commitment to React Native, estimating that the benefit/cost ratio of maintaining native codebases across mobile platforms was now above that of using an abstraction layer.
The about-face shift comes after Shopify declared in 2020 that React Native was the future of its mobile architecture, reaffirming again in 2025 its commitment after a successful 5-year migration of all its apps to React Native.
The rationale then was three-fold: stop building the same features twice, talent portability, and spending more time delivering value to users vs. chasing feature parity. Shopify at the time reported increased development productivity with apps that were both blazing-fast (<500ms screen loads) and stable (>99.9% crash-free sessions). Reactive Native features such as hot reloading and TypeScript were also mentioned as notable productivity enablers.
Yet, even then, Shopify did not discard native platform development entirely:
Native is still the best way for building cutting-edge features that leverage device hardware like 2D / 3D scanning and running AI models on-device. It is also better suited for building features that have memory limitations like home and lock screen widgets, Apple Watch apps and complications, App Intents, and Siri Shortcuts.
Native is also the better choice for long-running background jobs.
Instead of thinking native or React Native, think native and React Native.
A little over a year later, Shopify has now reassessed its technological choices, driven in particular by two key factors. The first was a looming significant refactor to adopt React Native’s New Architecture:
That work would have required us to revisit native module integrations, rendering, and the boundaries between shared and platform-specific code
Shopify was thus faced with a major engineering effort that made a deeper analysis of engineering options worthwhile.
The second factor was the fast-paced improvement in quality of AI coding models, agents, and harnesses. After a successful proof of concept led by a single engineer in just one week, six engineers rebuilt the flagship Shop app from the ground up to production deployment in 12 weeks, further reinforcing the clean-slate greenfield rewrite option over a migration.
By standardizing on modern declarative UI frameworks—Apple’s SwiftUI and Google’s Jetpack Compose—the team leveraged structural and mental model symmetries between platforms to guide autonomous agents while matching platform-native idioms.
Shopify reports improvement in cold startup latency (dropping 23% on iOS and 50% on Android), session stability (from 99.5% to 99.95%, i,e, a 10x reduction in sessions that crash), 75% faster release build times on Android. Also on Android, native feed scrolling maintained sustained 120 FPS throughput without requiring extensive manual optimization.
(Native vs. React Native comparison on Android. Source: Migrating Shop app from React Native to native)
In spite of the progress in AI coding models, the rewrite did still require considerable engineering involvement in architecture, planning agent work, validating task completion and remediating errors. Developers are encouraged to read both published in-depth articles.
An interesting detail however is that Shopify isolated the factors of change (the mobile platform, the UI) from the core, stable business logic and application state management to mitigate the slow feedback loops inherent to mobile simulators. AI models would thus dispatch actions, manipulate navigation state, and assert outcomes in milliseconds, on the desktop, without rendering UI or using a simulator. Simulators are reserved primarily for automated end-to-end integration passes.
The announcement unsurprisingly led to extensive debate in the mobile development community. One argument is that Shopify’s reported performance and productivity results are measured vs. the old React Native architecture instead of the new one, leaving open the possibility that migrating to the new architecture may have achieved similar or better results. Another significant tradeoff reported by developers is the difficulty of over-the-air updates when going full Native. Shipping a new version of the app may require going through the app review process gate, thus slowing down release frequency. One developer wondered if this being perceived as a strong argument in favor of React Native is not influenced by a web culture that contrasts significantly with the native development ethos:
I’ve worked with both native and cross-platform. I think the mentality of being able to make changes quickly without much review often comes from cross-platform, especially when the developers come from a web background.
Changes are cheap and fast, so teams often feel less pressure to test everything thoroughly before a release. […]
With native, you know each release is harder to roll back, so you tend to build more tooling around releases, think through changes more carefully, and test more thoroughly before they’re ready to ship. You opt for one bigger, more stable release every few weeks instead.
At the end of the day, both approaches work.
Shopify plans to complete its Point of Sale, and Inbox apps over the coming year, with the Shopify app (with 300+ screens, home & lockscreen widgets, Apple Watch app, Siri Shortcuts) due to completion this year.

articles.title: Google Home passe au MCP et laisse Claude et ChatGPT piloter votre maison, mais sous conditions — Frandroid
articles.text:
Voilà un changement qui compte et qui est dans l’ère du temps. La promesse de Google : confier les clés de sa maison à l’agent IA de son choix.
    Pour aller plus loin
            Le MCP est l’USB-C de l’IA, et c’est la seule révolution qui compte vraiment
            
La liste des IA compatibles ne se limite pas à Claude et ChatGPT, on y trouve aussi des noms plus obscurs comme Hermes, OpenClaw ou Google Antigravity. Dans les faits, il faut d’abord créer un projet Google Cloud, le configurer pour Home MCP, puis autoriser l’agent à se connecter. Et l’accès reste réservé aux abonnés Google Home Premium Advanced, la formule à 20 dollars par mois (environ 18 €), uniquement aux États-Unis.
Protégez votre vie numérique et vos appareils contre les virus, arnaques, ransomwares et menaces en ligne avec Bitdefender, primé pour sa protection et compatible avec Windows, Mac, Android et iOS.
Le Model Context Protocol, ou MCP, est un protocole standardisé qui sert de passerelle entre un agent IA et un service. En gros, il donne à l’IA un langage commun pour lire des données et déclencher des actions. Branché sur Google Home, il permet de consulter les résumés de vos caméras, de suivre l’activité de vos capteurs, de commander vos appareils ou de vous construire un tableau de bord domotique sur mesure. Google avait déjà glissé son IA Gemini dans ses caméras et enceintes ; cette fois, il ouvre la porte aux IA des autres.
Le périmètre couvre tout l’écosystème Google Home : thermostats et sonnettes Nest, mais aussi les ampoules et prises estampillées « Works with Google Home » ou Matter.
MCP s’impose, Google suit le mouvement
Si Google lâche du lest, c’est qu’il n’a pas vraiment le choix. Le MCP, lancé par Anthropic, a été repris par OpenAI puis par une bonne partie du secteur. Google l’a lui-même intégré à son Agent Development Kit (ADK), la boîte à outils maison pour bâtir des agents. Rester fermé pendant que ce standard s’installe partout revenait à se mettre hors jeu dans la bataille de l’IA agentique.
    Pour aller plus loin
            Alexa Plus débarque officiellement en France : Amazon propulse son assistant vocal par l’IA générative
            
En face, Amazon pousse Alexa+, sa version d’assistant dopée à l’IA, et Apple garde HomeKit soigneusement verrouillé. Google, lui, a perdu du terrain sur la maison connectée ces dernières années. Son ouverture ressemble autant à une contrainte qu’à un moyen de reprendre la main.
Vos données du foyer, nouveau terrain de jeu
Il y a quand même un angle mort. Un agent tiers qui accède à vos historiques de présence, à votre consommation électrique et aux commandes de vos appareils, ça élargit mécaniquement la surface d’attaque. Les garanties imposées aux développeurs, validation ou contrôle de sécurité, ne sont pas détaillées pour l’instant. Et la maison n’est qu’un front parmi d’autres : la même semaine, Meta a ouvert WhatsApp Business aux agents IA via un serveur MCP bâti sur le même principe.
Les bricoleurs de la domotique, eux, n’ont pas attendu Google pour confier leur installation à une IA.

articles.title: Apple TV lands in Nigeria for ₦1,300 a month: Here's what you get
articles.text:
Apple TV is coming to Nigeria for the first time, with access bundled into an expanded iCloud+ subscription starting at ₦1,300 a month. The service will launch in Nigeria before the end of September 2026.
The new iCloud+ plan goes beyond cloud storage, bundling Apple TV, Apple Arcade, Apple Music Select, and cloud storage into one subscription. Subscribers can also share the plan with up to five family members at no extra cost.
Apple announced the Nigerian rollout on September 15 as part of a bigger expansion covering more than 100 countries. The move adds 59 new markets for Apple TV, bringing the service’s global reach to 170 countries.
Here, Apple TV refers to Apple’s video streaming service, previously called Apple TV+. It is separate from Apple TV 4K, the physical streaming box Apple sells.
When does Apple TV launch in Nigeria
Apple says the bundle will reach Nigeria before the end of September 2026, but it has not shared an exact date yet.
The rollout will likely happen in stages, so you might see the new benefits before some other users do. To check your own status, open Settings, tap your name, select Subscriptions, and open iCloud+. Apple TV and Apple Arcade will show up there once your account gets access.
Nigerians are getting official access to Apple TV seven years after it first launched worldwide on November 1, 2019. The Apple TV app was already available locally, but the streaming subscription and its catalogue were not.
How much will Apple TV cost in Nigeria
You get Apple TV through an iCloud+ plan instead of a separate streaming subscription. Prices start at ₦1,300 a month for the 50GB plan.
Apple has confirmed five paid iCloud+ plans for Nigeria:
| iCloud+ plan | Monthly price | 
| 50GB | ₦1,300 | 
| 200GB | ₦4,500 | 
| 2TB | ₦14,900 | 
| 6TB | ₦39,900 | 
| 12TB | ₦66,900 | 
Every paid plan includes Apple TV and Apple Arcade, and you can share any of them with up to five other people through Family Sharing at no extra cost. The free 5GB iCloud plan does not include Apple TV or Apple Arcade.
What the ₦1,300 plan includes
- Apple TV
- Apple Arcade
- 50GB of cloud storage
- Apple Music Select
- iCloud Private Relay
- Hide My Email
- Custom email domain
- HomeKit Secure Video support for one camera
- Full access to Apple Invites
- Family Sharing with up to five other people
The 200GB plan adds HomeKit Secure Video support for five cameras. Plans from 2TB and above support an unlimited number of compatible HomeKit cameras.
At ₦1,300 a month, Apple’s entry plan costs less than Netflix’s cheapest Nigerian plan, which starts at ₦2,500. The comparison isn’t exact, since Netflix is a dedicated video service and Apple’s plan bundles a smaller show catalogue with cloud storage, games, and privacy tools.
What you can watch on Apple TV
Apple TV gives you access to hundreds of Apple Original films, series, documentaries, comedies, and children’s shows, with new releases every week.
Titles Apple is promoting as part of the service include:
- Ted Lasso
- The Studio
- Severance
- Pluribus
- CODA
- F1
Apple says its original films, documentaries, and series have won more than 900 awards and earned over 3,800 nominations since the service launched in 2019.
You can watch through the Apple TV app on supported devices or through a browser at tv.apple.com. You do not need an Apple TV 4K box or any other Apple device to use it. The service works on:
- iPhones and iPads
- Mac computers
- Windows computers
- Android phones and tablets
- Apple TV 4K
- Supported smart TVs
- Compatible gaming consoles and streaming devices
- Web browsers
Available shows and features can vary by device and country. The service also does not include third-party subscriptions or films offered for separate rental or purchase inside the Apple TV app.
Apple promotes live Formula 1, Major League Soccer, and Friday Night Baseball in some countries, but it has not confirmed which of these will show up in the Nigerian catalogue. Do not assume every US programme or sporting event will stream in Nigeria too.
Apple Arcade is part of the bundle too
Every paid Nigerian iCloud+ plan includes Apple Arcade, giving you unlimited access to more than 200 games. The games have no adverts or in-app purchases, and many work offline.
Some of the games Apple highlighted for the launch include:
- Football Manager 26 Touch
- NBA 2K26 Arcade Edition
- Madden NFL 27 Arcade Edition
- Hello Kitty Island Adventure
- Sneaky Sasquatch
- Angry Birds Reloaded
- Cooking Mama, Cuisine!
- Block Blast+
- Subway Surfers+
- Ultimate 8 Ball Pool+
Apple Arcade works on iPhone, iPad, Mac, and Apple TV 4K. You can find its games in the Arcade tab of the App Store or in the Apple Games app. Nigeria’s game catalogue may differ slightly from what other countries get.
The bundle also includes Apple Music Select
Your iCloud+ subscription in Nigeria also comes with Apple Music Select, a set of ad-free stations programmed by Apple Music. The stations cover regional music, current popular songs, and throwbacks from the 1980s and 1990s. You will find them under the Home tab in the Apple Music app.
Apple Music Select is not the full Apple Music experience. It plays programmed stations and does not let you pick individual songs, albums, or playlists. For that, you still need a full Apple Music plan.
iCloud+ subscribers get cheaper Apple Music plans
Apple is offering discounted Apple Music plans to iCloud+ customers in Nigeria. An Individual plan costs ₦1,500 a month, and a Family plan costs ₦2,500 a month. You have to buy these directly from Apple.
Add the cheapest iCloud+ plan and your combined monthly cost looks like this:
| Subscription | Combined monthly cost | 
| 50GB iCloud+ and Apple Music Individual | ₦2,800 | 
| 50GB iCloud+ and Apple Music Family | ₦3,800 | 
The full Apple Music plan gives you on-demand listening, editorial playlists, Spatial Audio, Lyrics Translation, and AutoMix. If you get iCloud+ through Family Sharing, only the person who pays for the plan qualifies for the discounted Music price.
How Family Sharing works with this bundle
You can share your iCloud+ plan with up to five other people, so one subscription can serve up to six people including you. Every member joins with their own Apple Account, and nobody has to share a login or password.
Apple TV and Apple Arcade become available to everyone automatically once they join your Family Sharing group. Sharing iCloud storage requires one extra setup step.
Your files, photos, documents, and viewing history stay private. The person who pays for the plan cannot open another member’s personal content just because they share the same storage.
The storage allowance is shared, though. Six people on the 50GB plan will split that same 50GB, so families that back up a lot of photos and videos may want to move to a 200GB plan or higher.
If a member already pays for their own iCloud+ plan, they can keep it or move into the family plan instead. Apple refunds the unused part of a personal subscription when a member switches. If the group starts running low on storage, every member gets a notification, and the person paying can then upgrade to a bigger plan.
What happens to your current Apple TV or Arcade subscription
Apple TV and Apple Arcade will no longer be sold as standalone subscriptions in Nigeria once this bundle arrives. If you already pay for either one separately, Apple will move you into iCloud+ and cancel your old individual subscription, since the service is now part of your new bundle.
Apple says it will send affected subscribers a push notification and an email explaining the change, and the switch should not interrupt your access. Your Apple Arcade progress and saved data carry over too.
If you already pay for iCloud+, Apple TV and Apple Arcade are added automatically, with no extra fee. Current Apple One subscribers keep their existing plans, though Apple lets them switch to iCloud+ from their subscription settings if they want to.
How to subscribe to Apple TV through iCloud+ in Nigeria
The steps depend on your device and software version.
On an iPhone running iOS 27 or later
- Open Settings.
- Tap your name and select iCloud.
- Choose Manage Plan if you already have iCloud+.
- Select Storage, then Get More Storage if you use the free plan.
- Choose a paid iCloud+ plan.
- Follow the prompts to confirm your subscription.
On iPhones running iOS 18.4 to iOS 26, open Settings, tap your name, select Subscriptions, and open iCloud+ to see the available plans.
On a Mac
- Open the Apple menu.
- Select System Settings.
- Click your name and select iCloud.
- Choose Manage Plan or Upgrade to iCloud+.
- Select a plan and complete the payment.
You can also buy or upgrade iCloud+ through iCloud for Windows, though Apple’s support page only lists iPhone, iPad, Mac, and Apple Vision Pro as devices where you can directly check your bundle status.
Once you subscribe, open the Apple TV app and sign in with the Apple Account linked to your iCloud+ subscription, or visit tv.apple.com from a supported browser. You will need a valid payment method on your Apple Account, and the bundle may still show” Coming soon” until Apple finishes the Nigerian rollout.
Why Apple is bundling TV and Arcade with iCloud+
This bundle turns iCloud+ into more than a storage plan. It gives Apple a cheaper way to bring its entertainment services to countries where Apple TV and Apple Arcade previously had limited reach.
Apple can now offer these services to iPhone users who already pay to back up their photos and device data, and it can attract new customers who see ₦1,300 as a low price for streaming, gaming, and storage combined.
Family Sharing could push adoption even further. If six people split the 50GB plan, its effective cost drops to about ₦217 per person a month. That storage does not split evenly by size, though, and 50GB may not be enough for six active users.
Apple also has room to sell more. Families can move up to bigger storage tiers, and iCloud+ subscribers can add full Apple Music at a lower price. Dropping standalone Apple TV and Arcade subscriptions also gives Nigerians one entry point for storage, video, and games instead of three separate ones.
Apple has not said that these business reasons drove the change. They are simply potential advantages of the new bundle.
How Apple TV Nigeria compares with other streaming services
The starting price makes Apple TV one of the cheapest paid video options in Nigeria. Netflix currently charges between ₦2,500 and ₦8,500 a month, depending on the plan.
Apple’s offer adds cloud storage and more than 200 games on top of video, giving it a different value than a video-only subscription. Its main weakness may be the size and local relevance of its catalogue. Apple TV leans on Apple Originals, and Netflix carries a wider mix of licensed films, international shows, and Nigerian productions.
Showmax, once one of Nigeria’s biggest streaming competitors, shut down on April 30, 2026, with MultiChoice folding its streaming service into DStv Stream.
Apple has not announced any Nigerian films or series as part of this launch, and that gap in local content may matter in a market that leans heavily on Nollywood. Apple’s sports offering also remains unclear. It advertises Formula 1, Major League Soccer, and Friday Night Baseball in other countries, but it has not shared a Nigerian sports schedule.
What this launch means for you
This rollout clears a barrier Nigerians have faced for years. You can now subscribe with a Nigerian Apple Account instead of switching your account region or using another country’s billing details.
Naira pricing also makes the cost easier to follow, though you still need a payment method Apple accepts in Nigeria.
At ₦1,300, the plan may appeal most to people who already need extra iCloud storage, since Apple TV and Apple Arcade come along as a bonus with no separate bill. The offer could also put price pressure on other streaming platforms, since Apple can support its video service through a wider ecosystem of devices, storage, music, and apps that smaller services do not have.
Apple TV’s success in Nigeria will still depend on more than price. Data costs, payment reliability, device support, and local content will all shape how many people actually use it.
What to know before you subscribe
- Apple has not shared one exact activation date for every user.
- ₦1,300 is the price of the 50GB plan only.
- The free 5GB iCloud plan does not include Apple TV or Apple Arcade.
- Every paid iCloud+ tier includes both Apple TV and Apple Arcade.
- Apple Music Select comes included, but full Apple Music costs extra.
- Only the person paying for iCloud+ gets the discounted Apple Music offer.
- Apple TV and Apple Arcade will no longer sell as standalone plans in Nigeria.
- Available shows, games, sports, and features can differ by country and device.
- Family members share the plan’s storage space.
- Family members keep separate Apple Accounts.
- Third-party subscriptions and rental or purchase titles are not included.
- Apple has not announced a free trial for the Nigerian bundle.
Frequently asked questions about Apple TV in Nigeria
Q) Is Apple TV officially available in Nigeria?
- Apple says Apple TV will become available in Nigeria through iCloud+ before the end of September 2026.
Q) How much is Apple TV in Nigeria?
- Access starts at ₦1,300 a month through the 50GB iCloud+ plan.
Q) Can you subscribe to Apple TV on its own?
- No. Apple TV and Apple Arcade no longer come as standalone subscriptions in Nigeria. Both now sit inside paid iCloud+ plans.
Q) Does the ₦1,300 plan include Apple Arcade?
- Yes. It gives you unlimited access to more than 200 Apple Arcade games.
Q) Does the bundle include Apple Music?
- It includes Apple Music Select, which plays programmed ad-free stations. The full Apple Music app needs a separate subscription.
Q) Can you share the subscription?
- Yes. You can share your plan with up to five other people through Family Sharing.
Q) Can family members see each other’s iCloud files?
- No. Each person uses a separate Apple Account, and their photos, documents, and other personal content stay private.
Q) Do you need an iPhone to watch Apple TV?
- No. The service also works on Android devices, Windows computers, smart TVs, consoles, streaming devices, and web browsers.
Q) What happens to your Apple Arcade subscription if you already have one?
- Apple moves you to iCloud+, cancels your old standalone subscription, and keeps your game progress and saved data.
Apple’s entry into Nigeria gives you official access to shows like Ted Lasso, Severance, and F1 for the first time, bundled with games, storage, and privacy tools. The ₦1,300 price looks attractive on paper. How well it performs in Nigeria will depend on the content available locally and whether Apple eventually invests in Nigerian and African productions.

articles.title: Meta dévoile de nouveaux abonnements payants pour Instagram, WhatsApp et Facebook
articles.text:
Si Meta a toujours assuré que ses services resteront gratuits, l’entreprise n’hésite pas depuis un certain temps maintenant à proposer des abonnements payants, pour échapper à la publicité ou pour bénéficier de fonctionnalités exclusives. Justement, Meta vient d’annoncer une mise à niveau de ses abonnements Meta One. Les abonnements Instagram Plus, WhatsApp Plus et Facebook Plus ont ainsi été enrichis de nouvelles fonctionnalités. Nous comptons aussi deux nouvelles offres pour les particuliers et quatre nouveaux abonnements à destination des professionnels.
Meta enrichit ses offres Instagram Plus, WhatsApp Plus et Facebook Plus
Les offres Instagram Plus, WhatsApp Plus et Facebook Plus ont été lancées en juin dernier. Elles sont aujourd’hui enrichies de nouvelles fonctionnalités. Instagram Plus permet désormais d’ajouter des polices personnalisées dans les messages privés et les Stories, d’envoyer des notifications lorsque certaines personnes consultent votre Story et d’afficher des aperçus des messages privés.
De son côté, Facebook Plus ajoute des options de personnalisation pour Messenger, offre davantage d’informations sur les Reels et étend les super réactions aux Reels et aux publications du fil d’actualité. Enfin, WhatsApp Plus testera prochainement deux nouvelles fonctionnalités : le stockage des sauvegardes de conversations et de médias, ainsi que les planifications de groupe. Ces dernières permettent de mettre en sourdine ou de masquer certaines discussions selon un horaire défini, afin d’être plus tranquille. Instagram Plus et Facebook Plus sont facturés 2,99 € par mois, contre 2,49 € par mois pour WhatsApp Plus. À noter que certaines de ces nouvelles fonctionnalités seront étendues aux lunettes connectées de l’entreprise.
Deux nouvelles offres : Meta One Core et Meta One Premium
Meta One Core, facturé 7,99 dollars par mois, propose la création et l’édition d’images ainsi que la génération de vidéos à l’aide des modèles Muse, une utilisation plus fréquente des outils d’IA intégrés aux applications, comme Restyle sur Instagram, ainsi que des effets vocaux sur Instagram. En d’autres termes, il est ici question d’une production de contenu multimédia plus poussée grâce à Meta AI. Cet abonnement intègre par ailleurs les fonctionnalités d’Instagram Plus, de Facebook Plus et de WhatsApp Plus.
Meta One Premium, facturé 19,99 dollars par mois, offre les mêmes fonctionnalités, mais avec une capacité de calcul plus importante pour les requêtes complexes et davantage de possibilités de génération d’images et de vidéos.
Quatre nouveaux abonnements pour les professionnels
Nous comptons au total quatre nouveaux abonnements destinés aux professionnels : Meta One Essentiel (14,99 $/mois), Meta One Advanced (49,99 $/mois), Meta One Expert (149 $/mois) et Meta One Max (499 $/mois). Ces quatre abonnements offrent aux créateurs et aux entreprises un niveau d’accès aux outils variable selon l’offre choisie, pour mettre en œuvre leurs campagnes de communication sur les réseaux sociaux de Meta.
À titre d’exemple, l’offre Essentiel donne un accès étendu à Meta Business Agent sur WhatsApp « pour répondre à vos clients 24h/24 et 7j/7 », tandis que les offres One Expert et One Max incluent « un accès optimal aux fonctionnalités et une capacité maximale d’agent métier Meta pour les équipes gérant des projets de grande envergure ». Enfin, Meta assure que l’expérience de base de ses applications et de Meta AI a toujours été gratuite et que cela ne changera pas.

articles.title: The US just admitted, for the first time, that it has weapons deployed in space
articles.text:
Why it matters: The idea of militarizing outer space is as old as the space race itself, but the US has not openly admitted to deploying weapons beyond Earth's atmosphere until now. While the confirmation was likely intended as a deterrent, the effectiveness of the Air Force secretary's vague statement remains unclear.
Air Force Secretary Troy Meink said at a Monday event that the US has deployed weapons in orbit to defend against hostile action. The admission crosses a new boundary following decades of peaceful international competition and cooperation in space.
Meink did not specify the nature of the weapons, according to CNN. However, the statement, made at the Air, Space and Cyber Conference in Maryland, remains significant because it represents a major shift in the US's posture toward outer space.
The declaration is likely aimed at China and Russia, which the US has long accused of developing and potentially testing military applications that could threaten orbital infrastructure. However, as a deterrent, its impact could be limited because other countries still lack a clear idea of the US's destructive capabilities in space.
While the statement is significant, it likely does not violate space law. The Outer Space Treaty of 1967 prohibits deploying nuclear weapons or other weapons of mass destruction in orbit but does not explicitly forbid conventional weapons.
Currently, the most viable theoretical space weapons would aim to neutralize communication satellites by jamming or destroying them. For example, Russia has previously warned that satellites supporting the defense of Ukraine, such as those used by Starlink, would be considered legitimate military targets. Late last year, intelligence services from two NATO countries claimed that Russia is developing a method of attacking satellites using clouds of tiny projectiles orbiting Earth at high velocities, but whether the country could deploy such a weapon remains unclear.
The US Space Force has also accused China of practicing coordinated satellite movements in low Earth orbit that it described as "dogfighting." Meanwhile, one theoretical defensive method might involve stationing a shielded mobile launch platform in orbit.
Outside of military applications, the Moon has once again become a major focus of the space race between countries and private companies. American and European space agencies, along with China, have spent recent years conceptualizing a lunar economy that could involve permanent habitats, data centers, power plants, and other infrastructure.

articles.title: Robotaxi de Tesla bajo la lupa: Elon Musk tiene fecha límite para justificar la autonomía del Cybercab
articles.text:
Tesla deberá responder antes del 30 de septiembre de 2026 a una serie de preguntas de la Administración Nacional de Seguridad del Tráfico en las Carreteras de Estados Unidos (NHTSA) sobre la autocertificación de su robotaxi autónomo Cybercab, como parte de una investigación gubernamental.
La agencia busca determinar si los controles para un conductor humano instalados de forma temporal, u otros equipos, fueron utilizados por la compañía como base para certificar que el Cybercab cumple las normas federales de seguridad para vehículos motorizados.
PUBLICIDAD
El Cybercab es el robotaxi de dos plazas de Tesla. El 3 de septiembre, la empresa inició el despliegue comercial de un pequeño número de estos vehículos en Austin, Texas, y anticipó una expansión gradual del servicio a más unidades y ubicaciones.
Qué debe certificar Tesla
La NHTSA pidió a Tesla que confirme si los Cybercab pueden ser conducidos por una persona y si la pantalla táctil incorpora controles que permitan a los ocupantes mover el vehículo.
La compañía también deberá informar cuál es la velocidad máxima de los robotaxis, qué límites geográficos y horarios tendrán y qué otras restricciones se aplicarán a su operación.
PUBLICIDAD
Según indicó la agencia, el Cybercab no cuenta con controles manuales convencionales, como volante, pedal de freno, pedal de acelerador ni espejos retrovisores.
El organismo regulador señaló que revisaba el proceso y los datos técnicos con los que el fabricante de vehículos eléctricos acreditó el cumplimiento de las normas federales antes de desplegar el robotaxi. Tesla no respondió de inmediato a una solicitud de comentarios.
Los cambios regulatorios para los vehículos autónomos
Tesla y otras compañías de robotaxis, incluida Waymo, de Google, respaldaron los planes del gobierno del presidente Donald Trump para modificar las regulaciones y permitir que estos vehículos operen sin volante, pedales de freno, espejos retrovisores ni otros equipos destinados a conductores humanos.
PUBLICIDAD
Los críticos de los robotaxis rechazan esas modificaciones y sostienen que las normas no deberían flexibilizarse hasta que las empresas demuestren que los vehículos autónomos son seguros.
En junio de 2026, la NHTSA propuso eliminar la exigencia de pedales de freno manuales en los vehículos autónomos, una medida que facilitaría el despliegue de unidades sin controles humanos en las carreteras de Estados Unidos.
La agencia también planteó otros cambios en las normas federales de seguridad para que los vehículos autónomos no requieran equipos adicionales de conducción humana. Sin embargo, las regulaciones vigentes seguirán en vigor hasta que esas modificaciones se finalicen, según informó la NHTSA.
PUBLICIDAD
Según la legislación actual de Estados Unidos, los vehículos totalmente autónomos no requieren la aprobación de la NHTSA si cuentan con volante, pedales de freno, espejos y otras características de los vehículos controlados por humanos. La agencia puede autorizar que hasta 2.500 vehículos por fabricante al año circulen por las carreteras de Estados Unidos sin controles humanos obligatorios.
En julio, la NHTSA aprobó una petición de Zoox, filial de Amazon, para el despliegue comercial limitado de sus robotaxis sin volante, una hecho que marcó un antecedente en la industria del transporte autónomo.
Qué características tiene el robotaxi de Tesla
El Cybercab de Tesla es un robotaxi autónomo diseñado para trasladar hasta dos pasajeros sin volante, pedal de acelerador ni pedal de freno.
El vehículo dispone de puertas de apertura y cierre automático, una pantalla táctil central y un maletero trasero con espacio para dos maletas estándar facturadas y dos de mano.
PUBLICIDAD
Tesla señala que la pantalla permite iniciar el viaje, regular la temperatura de la cabina, ajustar los asientos, controlar las puertas y acceder a música, juegos y otros contenidos multimedia.
Los usuarios también pueden operar varias de esas funciones desde la aplicación Robotaxi, que conserva sus preferencias de climatización y entretenimiento entre viajes. El modelo incorpora cámaras y sensores para circular de manera autónoma por calles, autopistas, intersecciones y estacionamientos.
Además, incluye una cámara interior para detectar la ocupación y prestar asistencia, un botón de detención para solicitar que el vehículo se detenga y puertos USB-C.
PUBLICIDAD
PUBLICIDAD

articles.title: U.S. and U.K.-based Expanse raises €4.5 million for predictive AI infrastructure platform | EU-Startups
articles.text:
Expanse, an AI infrastructure company, today announced a €4.5 million ($5.3 million) Seed funding round in order to expand its engineering team, accelerate product development and reach wider industry adoption.
The round was led by Crane Venture Partners, with participation from PXN Ventures, AIP Seed, and angel investors including former DeepMind researchers.
“Today, every AI workload begins with an educated guess,” says Ismaeel Bashir, co-founder and CEO of Expanse. “Engineers shouldn’t have to predict exactly how much compute their code will need before they press run. The machine should carry the uncertainty, not the person.”
Expanse’s Seed round can be placed amid broader 2026 investment in the infrastructure and software layers intended to make AI compute more available and efficient.
EU-Startups has reported London-based Callosum raising €85.4 million to route workloads across different AI models and chips, Vienna’s Ora Computing securing €3.5 million for model compression and inference efficiency, Helsinki-based Verda raising €100 million for AI cloud infrastructure, and London-based Nscale closing a €1.7 billion Series C for vertically integrated compute infrastructure.
Other adjacent rounds include €16 million for Switzerland’s AI Infrastructure Capital AG, €5 million for Danish AI infrastructure startup Velatir and €1.7 million for Prague cloud platform Zerops.
Together, these 2026 financings amount to approximately €1.91 billion, or around €1.92 billion including Expanse, although the total is heavily weighted towards Nscale’s round.
The UK is particularly represented in this group through Nscale and Callosum, the latter of which, like Expanse, is developing software intended to allocate AI workloads more efficiently across available compute.
Today’s news comes just one day after Crane Venture Partners announced their €419 million active across four new investment vehicles.
“The future of AI won’t be defined only by who builds the biggest clusters, but by who uses them most intelligently,” adds Scott Sage, co-founder and Partner at Crane Venture Partners. “Expanse gives organisations something they don’t have today: certainty. By predicting exactly what every workload needs before it runs, customers recover existing capacity, reduce waste and extend the life of some of the world’s most valuable infrastructure. We believe that’s a new and important category in AI infrastructure.”
Founded in 2025, Expanse’s software predicts what an AI workload needs before it runs, helping organisations reduce over-allocation, prevent failed jobs and unlock more value from the GPU infrastructure they already own.
Expanse was founded by four University of Edinburgh graduate engineers who previously built and operated large-scale compute infrastructure across quantitative finance and national supercomputing facilities.
While at the Edinburgh Parallel Computing Centre (EPCC), co-founder Ismaeel Bashir developed a multimodal HPC resource prediction system that predicted resource requirements across HPC workloads. Together, Bashir and co-founders Nikodem Bieniek, Eren Mendi, Yafet Melake recognised that even the world’s most sophisticated compute environments still relied on manual estimation to allocate resources efficiently.
Unlike traditional monitoring and observability platforms, which explain what happened after a workload has finished, Expanse says they work before execution begins. Installed directly into an organisation’s cloud or on-premises infrastructure, its models analyse workloads without code or telemetry ever leaving the customer’s environment, allowing organisations to optimise performance while maintaining data sovereignty.
Andy Barrow, Managing Director of PXN Ventures, says: “The widespread adoption of AI by businesses and everyday users has led to an unprecedented focus on the infrastructure required to service this technology and many of the challenges that engineers face. As Expanse has identified, one of those challenges is optimisation and helping businesses to make better use of their compute resource, which can lower running costs and increase scalability. PXN is proud to be backing Ismaeel and the team, who are tackling this head on.”
In one production deployment, Expanse identified nearly €6.9 million ($8 million) of idle compute capacity in a single month.
Expanse will use the funding to expand its engineering team, accelerate product development and bring its platform to more organisations across AI infrastructure, quantitative finance, life sciences, research and high performance computing.

articles.title: Após críticas, Amazon corrige bug de sideloading no Fire TV • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Após críticas, Amazon corrige bug de sideloading no Fire TV
Atualização no Fire OS desativou acidentalmente a instalação de apps de fontes externas.
Alguns dispositivos da linha Fire TV voltarão a autorizar a instalação de aplicativos de fontes externas. A prática, conhecida no meio da tecnologia como sideloading, estava bloqueada para muitos usuários após atualizações do sistema Fire OS liberadas pela Amazon.
Após uma onda de reclamações, a empresa reconheceu o problema e disse que a limitação não foi intencional. Na verdade, um bug no software, que já teve a causa identificada, será resolvido com um novo patch de correção.
O problema atingiu aparelhos rodando as versões mais recentes do Fire OS 7 e Fire OS 8 e afetou especificamente o menu “Instalar apps desconhecidos”. O sistema da Amazon passou a verificar desnecessariamente todos os aplicativos do dispositivo, incluindo os nativos, antes de gerar a permissão de instalação.
A interface nem sempre aguardava a conclusão dessa varredura, mostrando um menu incompleto ou completamente vazio na tela. Hardwares mais antigos e com processadores menos potentes, como o modelo de entrada Fire TV Stick Lite, foram os mais prejudicados.
A Amazon informou que o patch corretivo será lançado e instalado automaticamente nos dispositivos afetados nos próximos dias. Como a mudança afeta apenas o aplicativo de configurações do sistema, o número da versão do Fire OS não deve ser alterado.
Apesar do alívio para os atuais proprietários, a facilidade de instalar aplicativos de fora da loja da Amazon tem prazo de validade. A fabricante já confirmou que seus futuros dispositivos de streaming deixarão o Android de lado em favor do Vega OS, uma plataforma baseada em Linux. A mudança promete entregar mais fluidez e menor consumo de energia, mas impedirá o uso de pacotes de instalação no formato APK.

articles.title: John Ternus rejects the idea that Apple 'lost innovation' in one of his first sit-down interviews as CEO
articles.text:
'I don't think we ever lost innovation': New Apple CEO John Ternus defends Apple's track record as his first September launch comes to a close
The seat of innovation
John Ternus has barely been CEO of Apple for a fortnight, and he's already caused quite the stir. Some of this is to be expected; Apple's September event is barely in the rearview, and the dust has far from settled following the announcement of the long-awaited iPhone Duo.
Still, it's one small interjection he made in a video interview with TechRadar and Tom's Guide (see below) that tells me a lot about his relationship with the company he now governs.
In addition to discussing the new devices launched this week, we had the opportunity to ask Ternus about his views on AI, wearable tech and becoming CEO of one of the world's largest and most eminent tech companies; plus, crucially, his view on innovation.
When our Editor-at-Large, Lance Ulanoff, asked about his plans to reinvigorate the brand's image when it comes to innovation, Ternus replied: "I don't think we ever lost innovation."
Is it ever enough?
The unavoidable truth is that the "iPhone moment" is, perhaps, once in a generation; and there's a lot more competition in the playing field now than there was back in 2007. That being said, it's hard to argue that there's been no innovation under Tim Cook's tenure.
From Apple silicon chips (2021) and Touch ID (2013) to Face ID (2017) and the world's first over-the-counter direct-to-consumer ECG in the Apple Watch Series 4 (2018), there's been plenty to shout about — even though recent years have maybe been a little quieter, barring the Vision Pro... but that's not much to write home about yet.
Of course, Ternus' quick retort garnered some reactions nonetheless, with commenters across our TikTok and YouTube accounts arguing that true product-level innovation had been lost at Apple for many a year. So, what do you think?
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
Cook had a difficult job, without a shadow of a doubt: huge boots to fill in the wake of Steve Jobs' passing, a grieving user base and fanbase, plus lofty expectations to steer the Apple ship through everything from a global pandemic to hardware supply chain chaos; and that's just in recent years.
Apple's still kicking, with a strong set of products, devoted audience and a seemingly optimistic future under Ternus' leadership. Only time will tell what's in store for this new era after the iPhone Duo.

articles.title: Researchers swap in human brain cells for a mouse's cortex
articles.text:
In recent years, there has been a lot of excitement about the potential for studying human diseases in what are called “organoids.” These small patches of tissue, formed using stem cells, appear to produce many of the same cell types and at least some of the structures normally formed in actual organs, and thus can provide a better model for diseases that rely on the sometimes complex interactions among multiple specialized cell types that are a feature of the human body.
But even the most sophisticated organoids lack a lot of the features of a real human body. This is especially true for brain organoids, which don’t form any of the connections with specialized brain structures needed to behave “normally.” On Wednesday, a research group at Stanford University described a possible way to study brain organoids in a somewhat more natural context: They genetically wiped out a large portion of the mouse brain and replaced it with human brain organoid cells.
The replacements
Organoids, because they adopt a three-dimensional tissue structure and consist of various specialized cells, provide a much better model for an intact tissue than simply having a bunch of disassociated cells lying flat on a culture dish. But they still have a lot of limitations—they’re not hooked up to a circulatory system that allows the liver to process chemicals the organoid produces and don’t have immune cells moving through them, to give just a couple of examples.
This is especially limiting for studies of the brain, where any specialized structures are surrounded by structures that may exchange information with them, and often have long-range connections. An organoid is better than nothing, but it may not be a lot better if you’re interested in a disease that impacts communication among multiple brain regions.
One alternative has been to implant human neural stem cells into the brains of another species, where they’ll generally integrate into the nervous system and actively signal to their neighbors. But, given that those human cells are surrounded by the normally functioning neurons of their hosts, it’s not clear how much you can learn from this.
The obvious solution there is to get rid of the host cells and try to have the human cells take over their functions. But that option runs into all sorts of problems, largely related to the fact that the organism you’re implanting them into (generally a mouse) actually needs its brain cells. Human neurons mature much more slowly than those of mice and may not form the connections that are needed quickly enough for an animal that only requires 21 days of gestation. In the absence of normal mouse tissue, nothing would provide the human cells with the signals that help organize them into functional units.
The Stanford team decided to test a compromise and delete a portion of the mouse’s brain and put human brain organoids in its place. But they took a bold step and chose the cortex as the portion they would delete. The cortex handles many of the complex features of the nervous system, such as decision-making and memory, and its disruption would be expected to have dramatic consequences. Still, the researchers found a gene that is active in almost all cortical cells and used it to drive the deletion of a key gene that’s needed to separate chromosomes during cell division.
Amazingly, despite killing off most of the cells that should go on to form the mature cortex and cutting the brain’s volume in half, it was possible for the mice to survive this. The researchers had to eliminate most of the other pups to ensure the cortex-free mice got enough nursing. They left them with their mothers to nurse longer and then provided them with very high-calorie food. But these steps allowed nearly full survival of mice without much in the way of a cortex. (The mice were also immunocompromised to avoid an immune reaction to human cells, but this is less of an issue in a sterile mouse care facility.)
With that in place, the researchers then started implanting human cortex organoids into the area where the mouse’s cortex was no longer developing.
Partial recovery
A bit over 85 percent of the animals that were implanted with a human organoid successfully incorporated the graft tissues. Those went on to contribute 92 percent of the cells found in the cortex of these animals. So, it wasn’t a complete replacement, but the human cells largely took over the space normally occupied by the cortex. Once there, they formed all the major types of neurons that are known to be present in the cortex. So, all that is good.
The human cells also formed some long-distance connections, as evidenced by the fact that processes from human cells were detected as far away as the spinal cord. And the neurons did engage in synchronized activity spikes, suggesting a degree of coordination.
The less good is a general lack of structure. There is some indication of local organization, in that specific cell types that form within distinct layers of a normal cortex tended to be near each other in the cortex of these animals. But there was no sign of those distinct layers being formed, suggesting that larger-scale organization is lacking.
What does this mean for the mice? Overall, it appears that having a disorganized human replacement cortex was better than having no cortex at all, but not as good as having a normally structured one.
The researchers set them loose in an area with video monitoring and then used a machine-learning classifier to group similar behavior patterns. Normal mice and the mice that had their cortex eliminated showed distinct patterns of behavior. The mice with a humanized cortex formed a third cluster, distinct from the other two. Similar things were true with body weight: mice that lacked a cortex were much lighter than normal mice, but the ones with the humanized cortex were intermediate between the two.
Tested for memory in a simple maze, the mice without a cortex performed at a level consistent with random chance. Mice with the humanized cortex did better than chance, but not as well as normal mice. But on a test of the ability to form associative memories, the mice with a humanized cortex did no better than the mice with no cortex at all. On tests of fine motor coordination, the mice with the human implants were again somewhere between the normal and cortex-free mice.
What’s needed
The research team hasn’t described the sort of careful study of anatomy and development needed to draw any conclusions about what structures may be formed by the human cells once they’re within the mice, much less tried to quantify any variation among individuals that might give us some hints of what sort of capacity these animals might be expected to have. As a result, it’s impossible to associate the mild improvements that come from having the human cells present with any specific function they’re providing.
As a result, this isn’t yet the sort of model system that can help us understand the sorts of complex neural diseases that we might ultimately be interested in using this for. They do show that the human cells respond differently to brief periods of hypoxia, consistent with what we see in normal human cells. But that’s quite a bit different from showing that this is a great model for something like ALS.
There remains a chance that it ultimately won’t be—that the sorts of disorganized connections that do get formed in these brains will never make them a good model for human neural processing. But without further characterization of what the cells are doing in these humanized cortexes, it’s going to be difficult to know.
John is Ars Technica's science editor. He has a Bachelor of Arts in Biochemistry from Columbia University, and a Ph.D. in Molecular and Cell Biology from the University of California, Berkeley. When physically separated from his keyboard, he tends to seek out a bicycle, or a scenic location for communing with his hiking boots.

articles.title: CDPR Wants The Witcher 3 Remastered to Feel Like a Modern Release
articles.text:
Wednesday, September 16th 2026
	
	
	
	
CDPR Wants The Witcher 3 Remastered to Feel Like a Modern Release
CD Projekt Red wants The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt Remastered, launching September 29 as a free update, to feel like a game built in 2026, instead of a decade-old title with a fresh coat of paint. Speaking to PC Gamer, executive producer Jakub Kutrzuba explained that this overhaul goes well beyond the visual and technical bump the game got with its 2022 next-gen update. The team apparently reworked everything they could without rebuilding the game from scratch. Here's what he told PC Gamer about how far the changes have come:
"With the remaster, it is even bigger and it's also quite heavy, maybe even heavier on the technical level. But what is more important is that we are touching these aspects of the game which weren't touched since we launched it. I'm talking about the animation. I'm talking about the gameplay. I'm talking about the quality of life, how you actually play the game. We wanted to make it [comparable] with any other game which is launching these days. It's so easy to get used to these new improvements that it's hard to go back."
That last comment is also CDPR's own litmus test for success. If the studio's team can't stomach returning to the pre-remastered build, the assumption is that returning players and newcomers alike won't want to either. With all the changes, the remastered version does raise the game's minimum PC requirements considerably, though. The update was first announced at Gamescom alongside a teaser for the Songs of the Past expansion, and it will be free for all existing owners of the Complete Edition.

articles.title: AWS tells clients to quit Middle East data centers six months after Iranian drone strikes — Amazon offers no recovery timeline as UAE mulls underground data centers [Updated]
articles.text:
AWS tells clients to quit Middle East data centers six months after Iranian drone strikes — Amazon offers no recovery timeline as UAE mulls underground data centers [Updated]
Repairs are underway, but Amazon hasn't said when customers can expect them to be completed.
Update Wed 16 Sept 11 am ET: This article has been updated to clarify that AWS is undergoing partial recovery operations on its data center in the UAE. In an update to its dashboard, AWS says, "After a thorough assessment, we have determined that we are unable to restore access to the resources and data hosted exclusively in the mec1-az2 Availability Zone. We continue to work on recovering regional resources, as well as zonal resources hosted in the other affected Availability Zones (mec1-az1 and mec1-az3). Since the disruption began in March, most customers have been able to re-establish their operations in other Regions by restoring backups or copying data that remained accessible. AWS Support remains available to help customers who need assistance moving their applications to alternate Regions. We remain committed to supporting our customers in the UAE. We are working on replacing the affected infrastructure and will provide an update on the restoration of our services in the coming months. We have notified the relevant authorities and continue to work with them toward that goal."
More than six months after Amazon Web Services (AWS) data centers in Abu Dhabi and Bahrain were attacked by drones, the company has now had to tell customers to move their data to facilities in other regions. The Wall Street Journal reports that AWS has admitted that it's time for customers to jump ship to data centers located elsewhere in the world. In its AWS dashboard update, AWS confirmed "most customers have been able to re-establish their operations in other Regions by restoring backups or copying data that remained accessible. AWS Support remains available to help customers who need assistance moving their applications to alternate Regions."
The move comes as AWS continues repairs on the damaged data centers, but it stopped short of offering a timeline as to when customers can expect either location to be back online. AWS says that it remains committed to supporting its customers in Bahrain, but only said it would provide a further update early next year. It did not offer any specific recovery time frame for the restoration of services. Regarding the UAE, AWS says that it is working to replace affected infrastructure, but again only said it would provide an update on the restoration of services in the coming months.
Both affected data centers became targets for the Islamic Republic of Iran after the United States and Israel launched strikes on that country in February of this year. Months later, the Bahraini data center was struck by cruise missiles, and Iranian state media claimed it had been "destroyed."
The move is bad news for the United Arab Emirates. The U.A.E. has spent years trying to become a world leader in data processing, a pitch that led it to lobby U.S. officials to allow it to buy AI chips for its data centers.
Having made plenty of noise about OpenAI's decision to take a spot in a 5-gigawatt data center complex in May 2025, U.A.E. officials have since seen those plans stall. The WSJ points out that no lease has been signed well over a year later. OpenAI was expected to take 20% of the data center's total capacity, the kind of loss that is sure to sting officials if plans don't get back on track.
For its part, the U.A.E. is clearly well aware of the threat that the ongoing regional instability poses to its ambitions, and it's looking for ways to address the fears of potential partners. Officials have already hinted at the potential for underground data centers. While the move would make an already costly endeavor even more expensive, it could help defend new data centers from drone attacks. Building drone defense systems near data centers is another option.
Drone attacks can be catastrophic for any building, and data centers are no different. The data centers operated by AWS suffered fires and damaged infrastructure as a result of the strikes. In their efforts to fight the fires caused by drone strikes, emergency workers used water, causing further damage.
Get Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.
The Abu Dhabi and Bahrain data centers are relied upon by a variety of businesses in the banking and financial sectors. Those businesses cannot tolerate downtime, especially of the protracted variety. There's little sign of data centers slipping from the crosshairs of drone operators any time soon, either, and AWS is far from unique in finding its data centers under attack.
Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) claimed in April that it had hit a data center linked to Oracle in Dubai. That unit further threatened American tech companies, including Microsoft, Oracle, Alphabet, and Nvidia, this spring. It accused the companies of contributing to attacks on Iran. With that in mind, and with tensions in the Middle East looking unlikely to ease any time soon, it's perhaps unsurprising that AWS has asked customers to move data to safer data centers around the world.
